title: Des produits locaux et de saison à la cantine
content:
Quatre nouvelles communes de l’est du pays rejoignent l’initiative «Natur genéissen».
Depuis la rentrée, les maisons relais de quatre communes pilotes membres du syndicat intercommunal SIAS – Betzdorf, Biwer, Schuttrange et Stadtbredimus – proposent davantage de repas préparés à partir d’ingrédients produits par des exploitations luxembourgeoises selon des normes strictes.
Ce projet, lancé en 2014 par le syndicat Sicona et baptisé «Natur genéissen», connaît déjà un grand succès dans d’autres régions et ouvre une nouvelle perspective économique aux agriculteurs locaux.
Concrètement, les exploitations agricoles participantes s’engagent à respecter des critères stricts de durabilité et de qualité des produits, tout en aménageant des surfaces favorables à la biodiversité. En contrepartie, les cuisines des structures d’accueil des communes participantes qui achètent en priorité leurs produits. L’objectif étant de proposer toujours plus de repas sains, régionaux et de saison aux enfants.
D’ici 2030, au moins 15 exploitations agricoles de l’est du Luxembourg devraient ainsi accéder à ce nouveau marché. Le président du SIAS, Claude Marson, souligne : «Natur genéissen associe la protection de la nature à une nouvelle perspective pour les exploitations agricoles de la région.»
L’objectif est d’intégrer progressivement les 21 communes membres du SIAS à ce projet dans les quatre prochaines années.

title: Reserva em Minas Gerais reabilita animais silvestres
content:
Reserva em Minas Gerais reabilita animais silvestres
RPPN Jacob já resgatou e devolveu à natureza mais de 90 animais, com projetos inovadores de reabilitação, monitoramento e soltura
RPPN Jacob já resgatou e devolveu à natureza mais de 90 animais, com projetos inovadores de reabilitação, monitoramento e soltura
A Reserva Particular do Patrimônio Natural (RPPN) Jacob vem se consolidando como uma importante referência nacional para a conservação da fauna silvestre, especialmente dos tamanduás-bandeira, uma das espécies mais emblemáticas e ameaçadas do Cerrado brasileiro. Além dos tamanduás, outras espécies de animais silvestres já foram resgatados e reintroduzidos em sue habitat natural: 25 maritacas, 15 papagaios-verdadeiros, 9 emas, 9 araras-canindé, 14 quatis, 2 veados-catingueiros e 1 coruja-da-igreja.
Mantida pela ENGIE Brasil em Nova Ponte, Minas Gerais, a reserva abriga o maior cativeiro para reabilitação de tamanduás-bandeiras do país, um espaço com 2.500 m², onde os animais são preparados para voltar para a vida selvagem. A maioria dos tamanduás que chegam ao local são filhotes órfãos, resgatados após a morte da mãe em atropelamentos ou acidentes na região. Eles são criados no espaço e soltos somente depois de bem adaptados ao ambiente natural.
Desde que a reserva foi criada, cerca de 90 animais silvestres já passaram pelo processo de reabilitação, monitoramento e soltura e 14 eram tamanduás-bandeira. O recinto dos tamanduás conta com toda uma infraestrutura que imita o habitat real. Depois de soltos, os animais são monitorados por pelo menos um ano, com suporte de aparatos tecnológicos com recursos, como GPS e monitoramento por onda de rádio UHF.
Em 2025, a reserva passou a desempenhar papel estratégico na implementação de um protocolo elaborado pelo Instituto Chico Mendes de Conservação da Biodiversidade (ICMBio) para a reabilitação de tamanduás-bandeira resgatados ainda filhotes e submetidos a cuidados intensivos. A combinação entre o recinto especializado e o conhecimento científico gerado pelo Projeto TamanduAsas fortaleceu a RPPN Jacob como um dos principais pólos de conservação da espécie no país.
Além dos esforços de reabilitação e soltura, a reserva também participa de iniciativas de pesquisa e inovação voltadas ao monitoramento da saúde dos animais. Uma parceria entre a NobilisFauna, a Universidade de Brasília (UnB), a Universidade Smithsonian, dos Estados Unidos, e a empresa de tecnologia médica Medtronic, que possibilitou a implantação de dispositivos subcutâneos em tamanduás para acompanhamento de indicadores fisiológicos e de saúde, gerando informações inéditas para apoiar ações de conservação.
Com 358 hectares de área protegida, a reserva recebeu o nome em homenagem a Agripino Jacob, antigo proprietário das terras onde hoje está localizada a unidade de conservação. Em 2018, quando assumiu a concessão da Usina Hidrelétrica Miranda, ENGIE Brasil tem investido aproximadamente R$ 50 mil por mês na revitalização da infraestrutura da reserva e na construção de parcerias voltadas à pesquisa, reabilitação e conservação da biodiversidade.
Um dos principais marcos dessa trajetória ocorreu em 2020, quando foi estabelecida a parceria com o Instituto Estadual de Florestas (IEF) de Minas Gerais para o desenvolvimento do Projeto Áreas de Soltura de Animais Silvestres (ASAS). A iniciativa transformou a RPPN Jacob em um local de acolhimento para animais que passaram pelo Centro de Triagem e Reabilitação de Animais Silvestres (Cetras-MG) e estão aptos a retornar à natureza após receberem cuidados especializados.
No ano seguinte, a atuação da reserva foi ampliada com a chegada do Projeto TamanduAsas, desenvolvido pelo IEF com parceria da NobilisFauna e outros atores.

title: Rescatistas devolvieron a su dueña dinero hallado entre los escombros de Residencias Caribe, en La Guaira
content:
Entre los restos de las Residencias Caribe, en La Guaira, voluntarios encontraron dinero mientras avanzaban en labores de búsqueda y recuperación de pertenencias. En lugar de incorporarlo entre los objetos recuperados, decidieron localizar a su dueña y devolvérselo.
El hallazgo fue protagonizado por integrantes del equipo de rescate Máquina de Hierro, quienes contactaron a una mujer que permanecía en el lugar en busca de su esposo. El momento de la entrega quedó registrado en un video publicado por la periodista Maryorin Méndez, que compartió el diálogo entre los rescatistas y la afectada.
"Nosotros acabamos de encontrarte un dinero aquí abajo, mi vida. Queremos hacerte la entrega de este dinero", le dice uno de los voluntarios mientras le muestra los billetes recuperados entre los restos de la estructura.
Los rescatistas también habían encontrado documentos, prendas y otros objetos personales. Durante la conversación explicaron que fueron separando las pertenencias que aparecían durante la remoción para entregarlas a sus propietarios o familiares.
La mujer rompió en llanto al recibir el dinero y explicó que no se trataba de una suma cualquiera. Había pasado un año reuniendo esos ahorros con la intención de iniciar un negocio.
“Nosotros íbamos a empezar esa misma semana del 24, estuve parada un año guardando, guardando, guardando, para salir adelante y tener mi propio negocio”, contó.
Los voluntarios insistieron en que querían devolverle todo lo que pudiera recuperarse.
“Todo lo que salga de aquí está en ellos” le explicaron, mientras continuaban revisando los restos en busca de documentos y objetos que pudieran pertenecer a las familias afectadas.
Labores de rescate continúan tres meses después de los terremotos
El episodio ocurrió casi tres meses después de los terremotos del 24 de junio que devastaron zonas de La Guaira y dejaron miles de víctimas y cientos de estructuras colapsadas. El paso del tiempo no ha significado el cierre de las labores en todos los puntos afectados: en Caribe todavía permanecen equipos dedicados a la remoción y búsqueda de víctimas y pertenencias.
Este lunes, por ejemplo, voluntarios del Campamento Madrid reportaron que mantienen las labores de rescate y remoción de escombros en la zona. El grupo reúne a 29 rescatistas procedentes de otros lugares del país.
La búsqueda no se limita a los restos humanos. A medida que se remueve el material de las edificaciones destruidas aparecen documentos, fotografías, ropa y otros objetos que alguna vez formaron parte de la vida cotidiana de quienes habitaban esos edificios. La magnitud de los escombros ha convertido su clasificación y retiro en uno de los grandes desafíos de la recuperación.

title: Scientists identify first new wild cat species in more than a century
content:
Named Leopardus tilcayo, the small spotted cat lives in the Yungas cloud forests on the eastern slopes of the Andes. It is smaller than an average domestic cat, measuring about 18 inches from head to the end of its body and weighing roughly 1.36 kg (3 pounds).
The discovery began in 2016, when Bolivian biologist and National Geographic Explorer Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz was called to the Senda Verde Wildlife Sanctuary after a local man brought in what he believed was a domestic kitten.
The animal had been found on a road near a forest and raised for about a year. Its owner eventually realized that it was wild and could not care for it.
Read also : New Zealand’s endangered kākāpō population reaches 325 after record breeding season
Nogales-Ascarrunz initially believed the cat belonged to Leopardus tigrinus, a species commonly known as the tiger cat, oncilla or little spotted cat.
But in 2019, while preparing a guide to Bolivia’s wild cats, she noticed that the animal’s large rosettes did not match those of tiger cats shown in reference material from neighboring Brazil.
Further genetic research eventually confirmed that the animal belonged to a distinct lineage. Researchers analyzed genetic material from the sanctuary cat and another individual that later arrived at Senda Verde. The two animals were found to belong to the same species, which diverged from other tiger cat lineages about 1.4 million years ago. The findings were published Thursday in the journal Current Biology.
The scientific name Leopardus tilcayo comes from the name used by local communities for the animal. Nogales-Ascarrunz said people in the area have known the cat as a “tilcayo” for generations, although they do not associate the word with a particular meaning in Spanish or local Indigenous languages. The researchers chose to preserve the traditional name rather than give the species a new one.
The discovery also changes scientists’ understanding of tiger cats. The new study identifies five distinct tiger cat species in South America, showing that what was once considered a single species was actually a complex of genetically distinct lineages.
Small wild cats are difficult to study because they are elusive and often inhabit remote forests. Physical characteristics such as coat patterns, tail length and teeth can help distinguish species, but the researchers used genomic analysis to establish the tilcayo’s distinct position on the cat family tree.
Read also : Casablanca: Five Pumas have landed in Aïn Sebaâ Zoo—and you can see them from July 20
The team analyzed the genomes of 38 cats, including 26 Leopardus specimens. Unlike some recently recognized mammals that were split from already known species, L. tilcayo had not previously been identified by scientists. Researchers found no museum specimens that had been collected and identified as the species.
Its population in the wild remains unknown.
Nogales-Ascarrunz is now working to install camera traps in the Yungas forests to find more evidence of the species and determine how many tilcayos remain.
The researchers say the discovery also highlights the need to protect the Yungas, where development and agriculture are putting pressure on habitats used by tiger cats and other wildlife.

title: С 2007 года в море сбросили 500 тысяч тонн ракушек: в воде начались удивительные изменения
content:
Власти Флориды сбросили в Мексиканский залив более полумиллиона тонн использованных раковин устриц и моллюсков. Вместо загрязнения это вызвало настоящий природный бум: на побережье появились новые рифы, а вода стала значительно чище. Об этом сообщает The Economic Times.
С 2007 по 2024 год раковины собирали в ресторанах морепродуктов и на перерабатывающих предприятиях – вместо того чтобы отправлять их на свалки, их возвращали морю.
За те годы популяция местных моллюсков катастрофически сократилась: по данным NOAA Fisheries, исторические запасы уменьшились на 85% и более из-за чрезмерного вылова, штормов и масштабного разлива нефти Deepwater Horizon. Особенно пострадал залив Апалачикола, который когда-то считался главным источником устриц в штате, но в 2013 году был признан зоной бедствия.
Оказавшись под водой, старые раковины превращаются в основу для нового рифа. Молодые устрицы от природы стремятся прикрепляться именно к другим устричным раковинам – и чем больше их оседает, тем быстрее разрастается риф, создавая убежище и для других морских обитателей.
По данным NOAA, устричные рифы служат средой обитания и "детским садом" для крабов, креветок и рыбы. Кроме того, одна-единственная устрица способна фильтровать до 50 галлонов воды в сутки, снижая уровень водорослей и избыточных питательных веществ. Также рифы защищают береговую линию: исследования в заливе показали, что они способны гасить энергию волн на 76–99%.
Залив подает признаки восстановления
Эта работа – часть более масштабной программы по восстановлению поврежденных экосистем Мексиканского залива. После пятилетней паузы в январе 2026 года в заливе Апалачикола возобновили ограниченный вылов устриц. Только за 2024 год в штате сформировали 77 акров нового рифа, а долгосрочная цель – восстановить 2000 акров устричных рифов к 2032 году.
Впрочем, ученые предупреждают, что быстрых результатов ждать не стоит. Эксперт природоохранной организации Pew Чед Хансон отметил, что восстановление среды обитания устриц занимает десятилетия, а не годы.
Удивительные находки на дне океана
Напомним, подводный мир продолжает удивлять ученых новыми находками. Так, у побережья Аляски исследователи обнаружили сразу 9 новых видов глубоководных губок – благодаря этому общее количество известных видов губок в регионе возросло до 232. Как и устричные рифы, эти морские организмы играют важную роль экосистемных "строителей".

title: Salvar de la ruina la casa del bandolero más legendario: "Es una de las masías más icónicas de Catalunya"
content: La 'Caçadora de Masies' trata de rescatar de un abandono que parecía inevitable la imponente finca donde nació el temido y admirado Serrallonga, un lugar con 800 años de historia La cazadora de las masías, un patrimonio en peligro de extinción: "La mayoría no están protegidas" Joan Sala i Ferrer Serrallonga, probablemente el bandolero sobre el que más se ha escrito y cantado en Catalunya, nació en una imponente masía donde hoy ya no vive nadie. Es la Sala de Viladrau, una antigua casa señorial de 800 años, situada a las puertas del Parque Natural del Montseny. Desde hace unos años, un grupo de activistas por el patrimonio se ha propuesto una misión: salvarla del abandono. La historia de La Sala de Viladrau se remonta al menos al año 1226, cuando aparece documentada como cesión de un clérigo local. Levantada sobre un pequeño montículo, perteneció a la familia Sala, la del bandolero Serrallonga, hasta el 1645. Con los siglos, se fue ampliando, entre otros elementos, con una torre defensiva que le valió la declaración de Bien Cultural de Interés Nacional (BCIN). “Es una de las masías más icónicas de Catalunya”, reivindica Marta Lloret, técnica de patrimonio y presidenta de la Fundació Mas i Terra. “Nació como residencia señorial, aunque en la época de Serrallonga probablemente ya era una casa de payés”, sostiene. Dedicada durante siglos a la ganadería y al trabajo de los bosques, conserva todavía estancias como la sala de amasado de pan o el salador, para almacenar la carne de matanza. La Sala de Viladrau estuvo habitada hasta 2004, y aún albergó la actividad agrícola y ganadera hasta 2019 por parte de un masovero (la figura del labrador que vive en una masía y trabaja sus tierras sin ser el propietario). Después, la masía quedó vacía. Una de las habitaciones de la masía La Sala Tres años desde que se cedió Poco después de que su último ocupante se fuera, Lloret se enteró de que el futuro de esta centenaria casa familiar estaba en peligro. Para entonces, esta técnica ya era conocida como la Caçadora de Masies, por la cuenta de Instagram con la que se dedica a rescatar del olvido este patrimonio arquitectónico. Quien la puso sobre la pista de la Sala fue nada menos que Quim Torra, el expresident de la Generalitat, informado a su vez por los dueños de la finca, que buscaban ayuda para revitalizarla. “Los propietarios habían contactado con algunas administraciones por si podían intervenir, pero no obtuvieron respuesta”, relata Lloret. No querían venderla, conscientes del valor histórico y cultural de la masía y de que el destino de estas transacciones suele ser la reconversión de este patrimonio en negocios turísticos, ya sean casas rurales u hoteles. Finalmente, los amos de la Sala cedieron su uso en 2023 a la Fundació Mas i Terra, que preside Lloret, un gesto que se vivió como una pequeña victoria por parte de los activistas por el patrimonio. Pero desde entonces el reto ha sido aún mayor: elaborar un proyecto arquitectónico y cultural para mantenerla con vida, y buscar financiación para las obras. Actualmente, se encuentran en este punto tras recibir finalmente el permiso de obras. Han empezado una campaña de micromecenazgo para conseguir 40.000 euros, una parte del coste de arreglar el tejado y otros elementos estructurales. El resto esperan cubrirlo con subvenciones. O con donaciones de algún mecenas. “Estaría bien que algún gran empresario comprometido pusiera dinero”, expresa Lloret. Además del proyecto arquitectónico y de restauración patrimonial, que han elaborado desinteresadamente, los planes de la Fundación Mas i Terra contemplan que la Sala pueda albergar un centro de formación sobre actividades vinculadas a las masías, además de una escuela sobre construcción tradicional. Pero también que tenga una parte de vivienda, para al menos una persona, y así preservarla como residencia. La leyenda que nació en la Sala La de Serrallonga es la historia de bandolerismo más célebre de Catalunya, hasta el punto de que ha inspirado obras teatrales y canciones hasta nuestros días. Lo curioso es que Joan Sala i Ferrer no era conocido por el nombre de su casa familiar, Sala, sino por el de la masía de la mujer con la que se casó, el mas Serrallonga de Querós. Nacido en el mas La Sala de Viladrau en 1594, en el seno de una familia campesina acomodada, Serrallonga acabó convertido en un bandolero temido, que asaltaba masías y caminos y llegó a asesinar a un vecino que lo había delatado. Escurridizo para las fuerzas de la justicia, contó con la protección de algunos habitantes de la zona. Con el tiempo, la leyenda lo convertiría también en una suerte de Robin Hood catalán, que repartía entre los más pobres el botín de sus asaltos, incluidos los dirigidos contra los transportes reales. Serrallonga fue capturado finalmente en Santa Coloma de Farners en 1633 y ajusticiado en Barcelona el 8 de enero de 1634, en una ejecución pública concebida como escarmiento. Su muerte no evitó que se agrandara el mito, y son múltiples las obras que han recordado su figura, desde El catalán Serrallonga y bandos de Barcelona, estrenada pocos años después de su muerte, hasta Alias Serrallonga (1974), de Els Joglars.

title: Haute-Savoie: de nouvelles aides débloquées pour éviter la fuite des soignants vers la Suisse
content:
Haute-Savoie: de nouvelles aides débloquées pour éviter la fuite des soignants vers la Suisse
Des aides financières d'ampleur pour faire face à la fuite des soignants vers la Suisse (et ses salaires). Au début du mois de septembre, la Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie (CPAM) et l'Agence de santé (ARS) d'Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes ont annoncé de nouvelles mesures pour favoriser l'implantation des infirmiers libéraux en Haute-Savoie et dans l'Ain.
Une aide de 45.000 euros est par exemple proposée aux premières installations dans quatre secteurs définis: les environs de Saint-Julien-en-Genevois, Annemasse et La Roche-sur-Foron pour la Haute-Savoie, et Gex pour l’Ain.
Pointant les deux départements "directement concernés par la proximité avec la Suisse", où la rémunération est plus avantageuse, l'ARS justifie ces révisions dans un communiqué publié le 9 septembre: "la situation en matière de densité d’infirmiers libéraux est particulièrement difficile, alors même que les besoins de soins de la population sont importants".
Aides au maintien et à l'installation
En plus de l'aide à la première installation, des contrats incitatifs sont aussi proposés pour le maintien ou la simple installation. Concernant les infirmiers déjà installés, ceux qui se maintiennent dans les zones en tension pourront bénéficier d'un coup de pouce de 3.600 euros par an.
Ces mesures, entrées en vigueur à compter du 1er septembre, portent un objectif double selon l'ARS: "faciliter l’arrivée de nouveaux professionnels et encourager les infirmiers déjà installés à poursuivre leur activité dans ces territoires".
La réforme apparaît en effet comme un impératif dans les territoires concernés: "Il y a eu une augmentation de l'attractivité de la Suisse. Les personnels paramédicaux qui travaillent en Suisse ont augmenté de 60% en dix ans. On avait donc besoin d'une solution pour inciter les infirmiers à travailler côté français", développe pour France 3 Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes Romain Henry, directeur adjoint de la CPAM de Haute-Savoie.

title: 38 villaggi della foresta pluviale sommersi da un lago artificiale: questo è il prezzo per salvare il Canale di Panama dalla siccità
content:
38 villaggi della foresta pluviale sommersi da un lago artificiale: questo è il prezzo per salvare il Canale di Panama dalla siccità
Migliaia di abitanti saranno sradicati dalle loro terre ancestrali, nella generale indifferenza. Accade nel piccolo villaggio di Limón de Chagres, nel cuore della foresta panamense e a est di Panama, dove le comunità contadine isolate alle foci del celebre Canale vivono della coltivazione di fagioli, mais e della vendita di alcuni prodotti lattiero-caseari di mucca.
“Autosostentamento, lontano dal rumore, con le nostre tradizioni”, dice Maricel Sanchez, portavoce dell’assemblea contadina di Rio Indio che fa parte della Coordinadora Campesina por la Vida (Coordinatrice Contadina per la Vita), un’organizzazione sociale e comunitaria di base composta da agricoltori, comunità indigene e gruppi civici a Panama, e madre di due bambine. Tuttavia, questa vita tranquilla sulle rive del fiume Río Indio “presto scomparirà, inghiottita dalle acque di un progetto di bacino”.
Proprio così: Limón de Chagres, con le sue 62 case in legno, una piccola chiesa coloniale, un cimitero, un centro sanitario e una scuola, sarà uno dei primi insediamenti sommersi dalla costruzione del nuovo bacino artificiale del Río India entro il 2028. In totale, sommergerà 4.600 ettari di terra e 38 villaggi.
Perché tutto ciò? Perché è necessario garantire acqua al Canale di Panama in un’epoca segnata da siccità sempre più frequenti.
La crisi idrica
Il Canale di Panama è una delle infrastrutture marittime più importanti del pianeta: collega l’Oceano Atlantico e il Pacifico e permette il passaggio di circa il 5% delle merci mondiali. Il suo funzionamento, però, dipende dall’acqua dolce. Le chiuse vengono alimentate dai laghi artificiali Gatún e Alhajuela, ma negli ultimi anni la diminuzione delle precipitazioni ha messo sotto pressione il sistema.
Nel 2016, 2019 e 2023 la scarsità d’acqua ha costretto le autorità a ridurre il numero dei transiti delle navi e a limitarne il carico. Il cambiamento climatico sta rendendo queste situazioni sempre più frequenti: nel 2026, anche il ritorno del fenomeno climatico El Niño ha contribuito a modificare il regime delle piogge, spingendo le autorità a ridurre temporaneamente il numero di navi che attraversano il canale.
Il nuovo bacino del Río Indio dovrebbe quindi diventare una strategia per garantire il futuro della rotta commerciale.
Migliaia di persone rischiano di perdere le proprie case
Il costo del progetto è stimato in circa 1,3 miliardi di euro. Secondo l’Autorità del Canale di Panama (ACP), saranno circa 2.500 le persone da trasferire (ma le comunità locali contestano questa cifra e sostengono che gli abitanti coinvolti potrebbero essere almeno 13.500). Un problema urgente, dunque, per le abitazioni, ma anche e soprattutto il rapporto con il territorio. Qui, molte famiglie vivono di agricoltura, pesca e piccoli allevamenti. Perdere le terre vicino al fiume significa perdere una fonte di sostentamento costruita nel corso delle generazioni.
Quando partiremo? Dove andremo? Chi costruirà le nostre nuove case? E di cosa vivremo una volta perse le nostre terre?, sono alcune delle domande sollevate dagli abitanti delle comunità coinvolte.
L’Autorità del Canale assicura invece che le famiglie riceveranno terreni equivalenti o compensazioni economiche e che saranno destinati circa 350 milioni di euro al sostegno dei nuclei trasferiti.
L’allarme degli ambientalisti
Oltre all’impatto sociale, il progetto solleva preoccupazioni ambientali. Il bacino del Río Indio si trova infatti in un’area collegata al Corridoio biologico mesoamericano, una vasta rete di foreste che attraversa l’America centrale e ospita numerose specie animali. Secondo gli ambientalisti, il nuovo lago potrebbe mettere in pericolo oltre 237 specie di uccelli, 35 rettili e 49 mammiferi, tra cui puma, giaguari, ocelot e il tapiro di Baird, il più grande mammifero terrestre dell’America centrale.
L’Autorità del Canale sostiene che saranno adottate misure di compensazione ambientale, tra cui il rimboschimento di un’area doppia rispetto a quella sommersa e interventi per mantenere i corridoi di passaggio degli animali. Lo studio definitivo sull’impatto ambientale è previsto per dicembre 2026.
Da oltre un anno e mezzo gli abitanti delle zone coinvolte stanno protestando contro il mega progetto, sostenuto, nemmeno a dirlo, dalle autorità locali secondo le quali sarebbe necessario per proteggere una infrastruttura fondamentale per l’economia nazionale e internazionale.
La costruzione del nuovo lago del Río Indio mette così il Panama davanti a una delle sfide più complesse dell’era della crisi climatica: come adattare le grandi infrastrutture ai cambiamenti ambientali senza lasciare indietro le comunità che vivono nei territori coinvolti?

title: Sanningskommissionen klar – Birgitta läser vittnesmål vid överlämnandet
content:
Sanningskommissionen klar – Birgitta läser vittnesmål vid överlämnandet
Birgitta Ricklund är en av fyra som ska läsa vittnesmålen, när Sanningskommissionens berättelsebok överlämnas nästa vecka till regeringen.
– Det jag ska läsa kommer inte från mig utan från oss som grupp; vi samer, säger hon.
Vittnesmålen kommer att läsas upp nästa onsdag, då Sanningskommissionen samlas i Staare/Östersund. Då ska samiska erfarenheter av den historiska men också nutida statliga politiken synliggöras.
– Det känns stort och viktigt, säger Birgitta Ricklund som är ordförande i Sameföreningen i Örnsköldsvik och själv har lämnat vittnesmål till kommissionen.
Berättelseboken ”Jag frågar marken tyst om lov” är en dokumentation, som sätter ord på historisk rasism och assimileringspolitik.
Upprättelse och försoning
Liksom i Norge och Finland är det meningen att Sanningskommissionens arbete ska vara grunden för framtida diskussioner om upprättelse och försoning.
Förutom Birgitta Ricklund förmedlas vittnesmålen av Hugo Bengtsson, Ella Ristin Rimpi, Peter Steggo och av Sara-Elvira Kuhmunen.
– Jag känner ju verkligen att det här får de inte släppa, för jag och många andra har ju blottat oss och lämnat ifrån oss en berättelse, säger Birgitta Ricklund.
Överlämningen sker på onsdagseftermiddagen på Gaskeuniversitete/Mittuniversitetet. Eftersom platserna är begränsade, därför kommer ceremonin att livesändas. Mer information finns på Sanningskommissionens hemsida.
Så arbetar vi
SVT:s nyheter ska stå för saklighet och opartiskhet. Det vi publicerar ska vara sant och relevant. Vid akuta nyhetslägen kan det vara svårt att få alla fakta bekräftade, då ska vi berätta vad vi vet – och inte vet. Läs mer om hur vi arbetar.

title: National Park Service director calls Yellowstone's wild bison recovery an 'incredible conservation story'
content:
A little more than a century ago, Yellowstone's bison were hanging on by a thread.
Today, thousands of them roam the park. And the conservation challenge has shifted from simply saving the herd to figuring out how to manage a thriving one.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS
During an interview with OutKick OutDoors, Jessica Bowron, acting director of the National Park Service, called the recovery an "incredible conservation story."
After millions of bison once roamed the Great Plains, the animals were nearly wiped out across their historic range. Rebuilding those populations, Bowron said, has taken decades of careful scientific work and cooperation among the Park Service and its Tribal, state, local and federal partners.
"To show up at Yellowstone today and have the experience as a visitor of seeing a wild bison in a functioning ecosystem, I don't know that we could have predicted that 100 years ago," Bowron said.
That's a pretty remarkable turnaround.
And now, Yellowstone's bison are helping build conservation herds far beyond the park itself.
Yellowstone bison are finding new homes
Through the Bison Conservation Transfer Program, Yellowstone works with Tribal partners to relocate live bison that have completed the necessary quarantine process.
Since 2019, more than 600 bison have been transferred to 29 tribes across 13 states, according to Bowron. More than 200 were transferred in 2026 alone.
"This is one of the coolest parts of this entire conservation effort," Bowron said.
Once the animals are transferred, she explained, each tribe can manage its herd according to its own priorities and sovereignty.
"It's a great example of how we're able to establish and expand conservation herds through that kind of partnership," Bowron said.
But conservation success doesn't mean the work is finished.
In some places, rebuilding the population remains the goal. At Yellowstone, Bowron said the challenge now is largely about managing the healthy herd that's already there.
"I think at Yellowstone, we're in the latter — figuring out how to successfully manage the herd that we have with all of our partners," she said.
At the same time, the Park Service continues to pursue live-transfer opportunities with tribes interested in establishing or expanding conservation herds.
A conservation problem you want to have
The Yellowstone story is also a reminder that conservation wins don't happen overnight.
Bowron said rebuilding bison populations has taken decades of scientific monitoring and cooperation among Tribal, state, local and federal partners.
WHY TED TURNER'S APPROACH TO CONSERVATION IS THE MINDSET AMERICA DESPERATELY NEEDS RIGHT NOW
And even after a species rebounds, the work changes rather than disappears.
For generations, the question was whether wild bison could survive at all in places like Yellowstone.
Now, wildlife managers are dealing with a very different question: What do you do when the comeback works?
Bison don't care where Yellowstone's boundary lines are drawn. They move across a massive landscape, meaning managing a successful herd requires cooperation among the Park Service and the many communities and agencies surrounding it.
But the fact that there is a healthy herd to manage — and enough animals to help establish conservation herds elsewhere — would have been difficult to imagine a century ago.
For anyone who's ever sat in Yellowstone traffic because a bison decided the middle of the road belonged to him, it might be easy to forget just how close America came to losing that experience entirely.

Today, seeing those animals wander through the park feels almost inevitable.
It wasn't always.
So yeah, you can definitely call it a comeback.

title: Eläimet | Uhanalaisen naalin pesinnät Suomessa onnistuvat nyt vuosittain
content:
Suomessa havaittiin tänä kesänä neljä naalin pesintää Enontekiön alueella. Pesissä todettiin yhteensä vähintään 11 pentua, Metsähallitus kertoo tiedotteessaan.
Naali on asettunut neljän viime vuoden aikana muutamalle perinteiselle pesäpaikalleen Enontekiön tuntureilla. Laji pesi Suomessa vuonna 2022 ensimmäistä kertaa yli 25 vuoteen. Onnistuneita pesintöjä on sen jälkeen ollut vuosittain 3–4.
Lisäksi yksi naalipari asusti pesäpaikkaa Utsjoen tunturialueilla, mutta pentuja ei havaittu.
Pohjoisten tuntureiden myyrä- ja sopulikannat ovat olleet tänä vuonna nousussa erityisesti Käsivarren alueella muutaman pohjavuoden jälkeen. Myyrät ja sopulit ovat naalin tärkein ravinnonlähde.
”Myyrien suurempi määrä on vaikuttanut positiivisesti naalin pesintöjen onnistumiseen ja pentujen suurempaan määrään. Lisäksi kohentunut ravintotilanne parantaa merkittävästi kesällä syntyneiden pentujen selviytymismahdollisuuksia ensimmäisestä elinvuodestaan”, luonnonsuojelun erityisasiantuntija Jukka Ikonen Metsähallituksen Luontopalveluista kertoo tiedotteessa.
Naalin pesinnät ovat onnistuneet tänä vuonna hyvin myös Norjan ja Ruotsin tunturialueilla.
Naalin paluu Suomen pesimälajistoon on pitkän yhteispohjoismaisen suojelutyön tulos. Suojelutyötä tehdään tiiviissä yhteistyössä Ruotsin ja Norjan kanssa.
Suomessa tällä hetkellä pesivistä naaleista lähes kaikki ovat Käsivarren lähialueille Norjan puolelle vapautettuja tarhassa kasvaneita villien naalien jälkeläisiä, tiedotteessa kerrotaan. Norjan Oppdalissa sijaitsee yhteispohjoismaisen naalikannan vahvistamiseksi perustettu tarha.
Kolmen viime vuoden ajan suojelutyötä on jatkettu EU:n Interreg Aurora -rahoitetun Felles fjellrev – Together for the arctic fox -hankkeen avulla. Hanke päättyy lokakuun lopussa 2026. Suomessa hankkeeseen osallistuivat Metsähallituksen Luontopalvelut ja luonnonsuojelujärjestö WWF.
Suomessa naalin suojelutoimista ja kannanseurannasta vastaa Metsähallituksen Luontopalvelut. WWF ylläpitää Suomen naalityöryhmää ja tukee suojelutoimia.

title: Harris County to spend $3M on community safety programs leaders say have driven down crime
content:
Subscribe to The Y’all — a weekly dispatch about the people, places and policies defining Texas, produced by Texas Tribune journalists living in communities across the state.
HOUSTON — As executive director of the Harris County Domestic Violence Coordinating Council, Barbie Brashear has directly seen how domestic violence programs have helped families.
She also knows the dire consequences of such programs losing funding.
Brashear used her experiences — both personal and professional — to spearhead the Harris County Domestic Violence Coordinating Council program, which she hopes will become a model for cities across Texas and the nation. The program is unique in that it provides money to families affected by domestic violence to pay for a range of expenses like rent, utlity bills and groceries — with no questions asked.
“We’re leading the field and other people are looking at us to see what we’re doing,” Brasher said.
The domestic violence council works alongside the Holistic Assistance Response Team, or HART, and Relentless Interrupters Serving Everyone, known as RISE, two programs that are part of a community safety effort focused in cities and counties that surroundHouston.
HART sends behavioral health specialists to crisis situations, reducing jail time and connecting individuals to care. RISE is a public health initiative that aims to reduce gun violence through community-led interventions, like hospital bed visits for gunshot victims. The Domestic Violence Prevention and Intervention programs focus on directing federal grant funds to survivors and increasing community-based coordination between partners.
The three community safety programs were created in the wake of nationwide protests following the death of George Floyd. The Georgetown Law Center for Innovations in Community Safety recently released a report praising the progress these programs have made in making Harris County and surrounding areas safer with funding, resources, and intervention.
In areas where RISE operates, gun homicide rates have fallen faster than they have in Houston overall. The county’s Domestic Violence Prevention and Intervention programs have helped more than 5,000 survivors. And HART has freed thousands of hours for deputies and EMS to handle emergencies and connected more than 5,000 residents to care.
The programs were at risk of ending due to federal budget cuts growing economic uncertainty has led to a drop in philanthropic giving. Last week, Harris County commissioners gave initial approval to spend $3 million for them using local tax dollars. Final budget approval is expected Thursday. Commissioners are also expected to increase property taxes by 7.6% to help pay for these programs and close a $180 million budget deficit.
“Domestic violence resources have never been resourced properly from the beginning, ever. The demand has always been much higher than available resources,” Brasher said. “[COVID-19] funding got us a little closer, allowed us to invent and support and build some capacity, but it didn’t get all the way where we needed to be, and now those dollars are pulling back.”
Harris County — the state’s most populous with with more than 5 million people — plays a unique role in the Gulf Coast region. Programs started there often spread across county lines. The regional approach helps smaller rural counties that can’t often pay for their own safety net programs, Brashear said. She said without additional support from counties or state lawmakers, the future of many community safety programs in the rural parts of the state is grim.
“It’ll wipe those programs out,” she said. “Especially thinking about the surrounding counties around Harris County because what happens in the domestic violence field is when those families aren’t able to be served in that county, they’re coming into our county to be served because there is nothing for them.”
Abbie Kamin, Harris County’s attorney said the programs are working.
“The issues of domestic violence, gun violence, and mental health are pervasive and impact every corner of Harris County,” said Abbie Kamin, Harris County Attorney. “This is exactly the kind of innovative and data-driven work that we strive for when building the infrastructure that connects people with the resources they need most.”
While these community programs have seen success, funding streams for community safety programs are getting cut from multiple directions at once.
Last year, the Department of Justice terminated 365 previously awarded grants, with about $500 million in promised funds evaporating and affecting more than 550 organizations across 48 states. The Office on Violence Against Women has delayed or withheld money due to new federal cuts and restrictions on grant funding. The DOJ canceled 59 grants under the Victims of Crime Act. The Centers for Disease Control’s Division of Violence Prevention has seen layoffs, making it harder for community programs to connect with the federal government, and COVID-19 funds are simply running out.
“I can’t express enough how dire the situation is right now and how critical it is that we don’t move backward,” Brashear said.
Harris County safety net programs face major cuts
In April 2025, the federal government terminated 365 previously awarded grants, with about $500 million in promised funds evaporating and affecting more than 550 organizations across 48 states.
The White House has proposed another $850 million reduction in Justice Department grantmaking.
The Trump administration’s stated rationale for the cuts and new rules was that the programs were “funding DEI and cultural Marxism” rather than helping keep Americans safe, but a Council on Criminal Justice review found that about 60% of terminated grants made no reference to diversity, equity, race, gender, or related terms in their project descriptions. The council is a nonpartisan group that focuses on criminal justice and public safety.
“Prevention dollars have gone away completely, so prevention efforts aren’t being supported; DEI is definitely not being supported, and there has been an entire shift in priorities,” Brashear said.
The federal cuts are wreaking havoc on community safety programs in Texas.
Brashear said their domestic violence organizations in Harris County and Fort Bend County have lost collectively around $4 million. She said the cuts are leading to fewer staff to run shelters and longer wait times for survivors trying to access services in a county that has the highest domestic violence rate in the state.
“That is years of wisdom and years of experience walking out the door, and the turnover makes it even more expensive for agencies to function,” she said.
The Houston Area Women’s Center Domestic Abuse Response Team, which is on track to help up to 5,000 people this year, is facing operational reductions tied to the federal reconciliation bill, the Houston Chronicle reported earlier this year. Despite additional support from the county, HAWC has said it has been forced to lean more heavily on private fundraising because public funding is in flux.
And the Fort Bend Women’s Center, attributed layoffs at his facility to widespread grant cancellations and cuts from the Trump administration.
Trying to get county support
Harris County residents and advocates at public meetings have pleaded with the commissioners to fund the programs using local tax dollars.
“These are not charitable extras; they are the basic infrastructure people need to live safely and with dignity,” said Swathena Ryan, a worker for a Harris County domestic violence organization, told commissioners on Tuesday.
Commissioner Rodney Ellis, who represents many of the county’s Black and Hispanic neighborhoods, proposed last month investing an additional $3 million in HART, RISE, and the Domestic Violence Prevention and Intervention programs, aiming to make these programs permanent as demand for their services grows with the population. He said the proposed funds will raise the total annual investment in these community safety programs to around $14 million, or nearly 1% of the county’s law enforcement spending.
Of the $3 million, about $1.5 million will expand HART into a 24-hour, seven-days-a-week operation with staff; $600,000 will expand RISE into one additional neighborhood and fully staff its Cloverleaf neighborhood team; and $1 million will sustain domestic violence prevention.
Advocates say the three programs have done enough to earn a permanent place in the budget. HART has freed thousands of hours for deputies and EMS to handle emergencies and connected more than 5,000 residents to care. The neighborhoods where RISE is located experienced a 36% drop in crime — including a 48% drop in family violence and a 34% drop in aggravated robberies — in the first two years after the program was piloted there. The county’s Domestic Violence Prevention and Intervention programs have helped more than 5,000 survivors and their children with resources to safely leave abusive situations and delivered more than 20,000 hours of therapeutic care to 1,000 families.
Ellis said that for Harris County to meet the demands of its growing population, it can’t just prosecute people; it must also try to help them, and that requires funding the systems that support them.
“We hope to make Harris County a perfect model for other people to look at when you talk about community safety, not just in the state but even nationally,” he said.

title: NWU graduate turns the mysteries of sleep into award-winning art
content:
A creative university project inspired by sleep paralysis has earned North-West University (NWU) graphic design graduate Ashley du Rand international recognition and demonstrated the impact of purposeful creative education.
Ashley was named the New Talent Winner in the publishing category of the World Illustration Awards, a leading international illustration competition. Her achievement is especially significant because 2026 was the first year that NWU entered the competition.
After completing her graphic design studies in 2025, Ashley continued her academic journey with an honours degree in art history. She describes the award as an affirmation of the value of her work and an important boost to her confidence.
Finding inspiration in the shadows
Ashley developed her winning project during an authorial illustration module, which gives students the freedom to create self-directed work around a subject of their choice.
Known for producing colourful and whimsical work, she deliberately chose a darker theme that would challenge her creativity. Her research led her to sleep paralysis, a temporary condition in which someone is conscious but unable to move or speak while falling asleep or waking up.
Ashley became interested in six unsettling creatures and legends associated with the condition across different cultures. Drawing on her love of character design, she reimagined these figures in her own visual style.
The result was a set of two graphic novels featuring frightening, dreamlike characters. Through visual storytelling, the works also explore ways of overcoming sleep paralysis.
Guidance that develops professional talent
Ashley credits her growth to the close guidance she received from lecturers in NWU’s Graphic Design subject group. One-on-one consultations, detailed critiques and repeated refinement helped her develop work that was stronger, more polished and ready for a professional audience.
Illustration art lecturer Danelle Heenop encouraged Ashley to enter the World Illustration Awards. She says the achievement reflects the subject group’s emphasis on combining design, illustration and industry-related skills to prepare students for sustainable careers in the creative industries.
Competitions form part of that preparation by exposing students’ work to industry professionals and helping young creatives build confidence. Ashley had already shown promise during her second year, when she was selected as a finalist in the Gold Pack packaging design competition.
She now hopes to pursue a career in character design and concept art, particularly in the gaming industry.
Ashley’s success shows what can happen when creative curiosity is supported by purposeful teaching and professional preparation. A challenging university assignment became an internationally recognised body of work, strengthening both her career prospects and NWU’s reputation for developing creative talent.
