title: A Farmer’s Son Saw His Father Struggle. Now He Helps 50,000 Farmers Earn From Solar Power
content: It is barely past dawn when Nikhil Patel reaches his field. For years, watering his crops came with a familiar worry. Would there be electricity when he needed it? Would he have to depend on the diesel pump again? This morning looks different. Rows of solar panels stand along the edge of his land. The solar-powered pump begins drawing water towards his crops. There is another change too: his farm can now earn from the sun shining over it. And Nikhil is not alone. Across Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh and Odisha, thousands of farmers are turning to solar power in similar ways. Behind this effort is Bhavesh Patidar, who grew up in a farming family in Khalghat, Madhya Pradesh, and closely saw how difficult it could be for a farmer to earn a stable income. He later studied at IIT and built a career in technology before founding Solarsure. Since its launch in November 2024, the company says it has commissioned over 300 MW of solar capacity and reached more than 50,000 farmers through its projects. ‘I didn’t research the problem, I lived it’ Growing up in a farming family, Bhavesh witnessed the uncertainty that defined agricultural life. His father worked tirelessly on the farm for decades, yet financial security always seemed out of reach. But there was one thing he heard his father say again and again over the years. “Pura jeevan kheti mein laga diya, par kabhi achhi kamai nahi hui.”(I spent my entire life farming, but never earned a truly good income.) The words lingered long after Bhavesh left home. Solar panels installed along the edge of Nikhil Patel’s farm now help power irrigation while creating another source of income for his family. They stayed with him as he went on to study at IIT-BHU and build a career in technology. He founded the agritech startup Neurafarms, which was later acquired, and spent years working with data-driven systems and climate-tech. But even as his work took him in a different direction, the problem he had grown up seeing at home remained familiar. “The problem was never something I discovered through research,” Bhavesh says. “I had lived it and seen it every day growing up.” Years later, the government’s PM-KUSUM scheme gave him a chance to do something about it. The scheme allows farmers to use solar in different ways, from powering irrigation pumps to setting up larger grid-connected plants and selling the electricity they generate. Bhavesh was interested in the latter: could the land itself become another source of income? He decided to test the idea on his own family’s land. Under the scheme, he set up a 2 MW solar plant and began selling electricity back to the grid. Unlike farm income, which could rise and fall with the weather and market prices, the income from solar was more predictable. Neighbouring farmers began noticing the plant and asking how it worked, and whether they could do something similar on their own land. That experiment eventually became ‘Solarsure’. Bhavesh launched the Indore-based renewable energy Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) company in November 2024. Today, it works across Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh and Odisha, helping farmers set up solar projects on underused or less-fertile land. Through solar projects, farmers can use underused or less-fertile land to generate electricity and supply it to the grid. Solarsure says over 50,000 farmers have participated in its projects, with company estimates suggesting income increases of more than 30 percent. So far, the company has commissioned over 300 MW of solar capacity and built a project pipeline exceeding 1.5 GW. What if farmers could sell power too? For many farmers, the definition of solar energy starts and ends with irrigation pumps, but Bhavesh believes the opportunity is much bigger. “Farmers should not only consume energy,” he says. “They should be able to produce and sell it as well.” Through Solarsure, farmers receive support at every stage of the process — from project design and financing assistance to installation, maintenance, and grid integration. The company develops both ground-mounted and rooftop solar systems while helping farmers access government schemes and financing options. Before a project is commissioned, Solarsure also uses AI and satellite data from agencies such as ISRO and NASA to study climate risks, wind conditions and long-term site suitability. The idea is to understand how well a site is likely to perform and optimise energy generation over time. Solarsure uses AI and satellite data to assess factors such as climate risks, wind conditions and site suitability before setting up solar projects. The company also provides the digital infrastructure needed for effective grid integration, ensuring that electricity generated by solar plants can be supplied reliably to the grid. For Bhavesh, all of this technology matters because of what it can change for a farmer’s income. “In farming, too much depends on factors outside a farmer's control,” he says. “Solar creates a second stream of income that is predictable and long-term.” ‘Now, I have a fixed monthly income’ Back in Nikhil’s field, you can see the transformation beautifully play out. A farmer by occupation, Nikhil first came across information about solar projects under the PM-KUSUM scheme through social media. Curious, he began researching the concept and eventually connected with Solarsure. At the time, financial pressures were mounting. “There was a money crisis,” he recalls. “I wanted to understand whether this could really work.” After learning more about the process, he decided to move forward. Looking back, he calls it one of the best decisions of his life. “Earlier, I faced many problems financially,” he says. “Now I receive a fixed income every month. My EMIs are managed, and I can plan for the future.” The additional income has also given him confidence to explore other opportunities. “Today I can make decisions easily. Whether it is for my family or a small side business, I have the confidence to move ahead.” For Nikhil, the solar project has brought a fixed monthly income, helping him manage EMIs and plan ahead for his family. For Nikhil, being able to plan ahead is perhaps the biggest change. And after seeing what solar has done for his own finances, he wants other farmers to at least understand the option available to them. “The weather is uncertain, and farming incomes are not fixed. If farmers want better earnings and a better life, they should understand solar power and explore the PM-KUSUM scheme.” While Nikhil points to a fixed monthly earning, another farmer, Mitesh, has experienced the financial benefit in a different way: through lower household electricity costs. Living in a 20-member joint family, he once paid electricity bills of around Rs 12,000 every month. After installing a 5-kW solar system, that figure dropped dramatically. “Today my electricity bill is only around Rs 1,000 to Rs 1,200. I save nearly Rs 10,000 to Rs 12,000 every month.” From paying EMIs to planning ahead For a farmer, an extra source of income can change very ordinary decisions. An EMI gets paid on time. An electricity bill no longer eats into the month’s earnings. There is a little more room to think about the next crop, a child’s education, or an expense at home without wondering where the money will come from. That is what makes solar interesting to Bhavesh. Farming will still depend on rain, crop prices and a hundred things a farmer cannot control. But the sunlight falling on the same piece of land can give the family something else to rely on. Sometimes that means cheaper electricity. Sometimes it means water for the field. And sometimes, as Nikhil found, it means knowing that some money will come in even when the farming season does not go as planned. From lower electricity bills to additional income, solar power is helping farming families find another way to make their land and resources work for them. This takes Bhavesh back to something he heard from his father for years: that a lifetime of farming had still not brought the financial security he had hoped for. Today, Bhavesh hopes he can help other farming families write a different story, one where the land beneath their feet and the sun above their heads can both help them build a more secure future. “If farmers can earn with dignity and build financial security for their families, then we've achieved something meaningful,” he smiles. All images courtesy Solarsure team

title: Kwara unveils cattle artificial insemination programme
content:
The Kwara State Government has commenced a statewide cattle artificial insemination programme targeting thousands of animals as part of efforts to improve breeds and increase milk and dairy production.
The initiative, being implemented in collaboration with Genex URUS American International Animal Breeding Company, began with 500 cattle in September, while the government hopes to increase the number to about 1,000 by the end of the year.
The Commissioner for Livestock Development, Oloruntoyosi Thomas, disclosed this on Sunday during the flag-off of the exercise at TGB Farms in Ganiki, Ilorin South Local Government Area.
Thomas said the intervention was part of the government’s broader efforts to transform livestock production in the state, adding that artificial insemination would help farmers gain access to improved breeds.
She explained that the animals had first undergone synchronisation as part of preparations for the insemination, adding that the programme would continue beyond the initial phase.
“One of the ways to improve breeds is through artificial insemination. We are going to inseminate thousands of cattle across the state.
“In terms of numbers, we are going to inseminate thousands. We are starting with 500 this month of September, but by the end of the year we are hoping to reach maybe 1,000, and then we keep going. It’s a long process, but we are just starting,” she said.
Thomas also disclosed plans to establish an artificial insemination centre in Malete, with similar facilities expected to be introduced in other identified communities to improve farmers’ access to the service.
She said the state was also developing local capacity by involving students of animal production and youths from pastoralist communities in the exercise.
“We need to ensure that we have well-trained technicians—artificial insemination technicians—and that’s why we are involving our students from the University of Ilorin and the various tertiary institutions in the state,” she said.
According to her, building a pool of trained personnel would help reduce the cost of the exercise, improve the synchronisation process and increase the chances of successful insemination.
The Director of Livestock in the ministry, Ahmed Umar, said the success of the programme would depend on the cooperation of stakeholders across the livestock sector.
Umar expressed optimism that the exercise would record an 85 per cent success rate, while calling for the support of farmers and other stakeholders.
“We want to develop this sector the way it should be developed by having improved breeds. This cannot be done alone. All stakeholders must come together to ensure success,” he said.
Also, the Team Lead of Genex URUS American International Animal Breeding Company, Saka Shittu, said the intervention was designed to improve the quality of cattle through the use of selected semen, particularly to increase dairy production.
“For now, the programme focuses on cattle; it will later be extended to other livestock. The essence of the programme is that animals are being inseminated with improved semen selected to boost dairy production,” Shittu said.
He urged cattle owners, including pastoralists and smallholder dairy farmers, to participate in the scheme, stressing that the service was currently being provided free of charge in Kwara.
Shittu added that each farmer was entitled to have two cattle inseminated at no cost, urging livestock owners to take advantage of the intervention.
The flag-off also provided practical exposure for students of animal production, with participants drawn from the University of Ilorin, Kwara State University, Malete, and Usman Danfodiyo University, Sokoto.
The delegation to the exercise included the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Livestock Development, Muhammed Yahaya; principal officers of the ministry; officials of SAPZ and L-PRES; as well as students and youths from the pastoralist community.
The Director of TGB Farms, Ishola Peace, commended the government for selecting the farm to participate in the programme.
She said the intervention would provide the farm with an opportunity to benefit from the state’s livestock development initiative.
An animal production student of the University of Ilorin, Owodunni Lawal, also appreciated the government for allowing students to gain practical knowledge of artificial insemination through the exercise.

title: Programme launched to support boys aged 12-19
content:
A new school-based programme has been launched to support boys aged 12 to 19.
The MARK programme has been developed to help boys speak about and navigate the pressures of growing up today.
It provides male facilitators to speak to young boys about the pressures they face, and help them to build confidence and a sense of belonging.
The programme was developed by the research body The Shona Project as a direct response to The Perfect Storm 2026 national survey.
Historically, the organisation has focused on the lives of teenage girls. This is the first time boys have been included in their research.
The survey intends to reflect the experiences of 802 12-to-19-year-olds in Ireland dealing with the pressures of adolescence.
MARK Programme Director Dónal Kearney said: "Through MARK, we are taking action and creating spaces where boys can reflect on and question these pressures in a non-judgemental environment. We want boys to know they don't have to figure everything out on their own."
The Shona Project said more needs to be done to ensure that young people get the support they need before "challenges become crises and struggling becomes the norm."
Seán Darcy is a MARK facilitator. He visits secondary schools and speaks to teenage boys about what masculinity means to them.
"It's more important than ever, to be honest, because I think young men are getting so many different messages about what it means to be a man, and how they should identify themselves," he said.
Nathaneal Wei Cassidy is a 16-year-old secondary school student.
He said that he doesn't discuss worries or pressures with his peers.
"Funny - I talk about it with girls but I don't talk about it with boys because it's just not the done thing."
Nathaneal welcomes the MARK programme, saying it is "an opportunity for boys to get together and talk".
The Perfect Storm Survey
Almost half of teenagers aged 16 to 19 say they are struggling with life, according to The Perfect Storm 2026 survey.
It found that girls tend to experience difficulties earlier in their teenage years, with 44% of girls aged 12 to 15 stating that they are struggling, compared with 24% of boys.
However, by late adolescence there is a decline in well-being for both genders, as 47% of young people aged 16 to 19 said they were struggling - 55% of girls and 38% of boys.
Future anxiety among boys more than doubles as they get older, but demand for mental health support increased by just 4%.
It said teenage boys are not more resilient than teenage girls, but that this "self-report may underestimate difficulties among boys as many find it challenging to express feelings or articulate difficulties."

title: Florida restringirá uso de inteligencia artificial en escuelas y universidades desde 2027
content:
Florida impondrá nuevas restricciones al uso de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en escuelas y universidades públicas, sumándose a las medidas adoptadas por los distritos escolares de Los Ángeles y Nueva York ante las crecientes preocupaciones sobre el impacto de esta tecnología en la educación.
El Consejo de Educación de Florida aprobó por unanimidad nuevas limitaciones a la IA en escuelas públicas de preescolar a secundaria y en las universidades públicas estatales, incluyendo prohibir esta tecnología para “satisfacer las necesidades sociales” de los alumnos o “simular amistad, compañía o relaciones emocionales” con ellos.
La normativa también impedirá que los alumnos empleen inteligencia artificial para realizar trabajos o evaluaciones calificadas de un curso o programa. Asimismo, restringirá el uso de sistemas con diseños antropomórficos o destinados a establecer relaciones que incentiven a los estudiantes a continuar interactuando con la herramienta.
- LEA TAMBIÉN: Los líderes de la IA piden reducir su desarrollo, pero la competencia dificulta el acuerdo
Las medidas, que afectarán a más de 3 millones de estudiantes a partir de julio de 2027, también obligan a las escuelas a obtener consentimiento de los padres sobre la implementación de estas herramientas y, si las rechazan, los planteles deberán proporcionar alternativas de enseñanza sin inteligencia artificial.
La alarma nacional por la IA
Las medidas de Florida contra la IA se aprueban semanas después de restricciones avaladas por los distritos escolares de Los Ángeles y Nueva York, los dos mayores de Estados Unidos, seguidos por el de Miami.
Mientras Los Ángeles anunció la prohibición de la IA generativa de texto, imágenes y otro contenido, Nueva York emitió una moratoria de un año de esta tecnología para niños desde preescolar hasta octavo grado.
Casi la mitad de los estados en EE.UU., 24, han emitido lineamientos para la IA en las aulas, según la organización civil TeachAI, mientras la asociación FutureEd ha documentado 77 proyectos de ley en 27 estados que abordan la inteligencia artificial en la enseñanza.
En contraste, el gobernador de Florida, el republicano Ron DeSantis, advirtió el lunes a los miembros de su partido que apoyar la IA será una “posición perdedora” en las próximas elecciones.
Con información de EFE.

title: Onderzoeksrapport Handelingsperspectief dankzij burgerwetenschap
content:
Wat burgerwetenschap allemaal teweegbrengt is niet altijd direct zichtbaar. Waag Futurelab onderzocht de mogelijkheden die burgerwetenschap biedt voor bewoners, overheden en kennisinstellingen. De publicatie Handelingsperspectief dankzij burgerwetenschap deelt de belangrijkste bevindingen van het onderzoek.
Burgerwetenschap is in opkomst. In heel Nederland zijn er gemeenschappen actief die metingen doen van de luchtkwaliteit, waterkwaliteit, biodiversiteit, geluid, bodem en allerlei andere aspecten van de leefomgeving. Steeds meer (lokale) overheden en kennisinstellingen werken samen met bewoners aan dit soort onderzoeken en maatschappelijke vraagstukken.
Burgerwetenschap levert niet alleen meer kennis op, maar brengt ook andere acties op gang. Toch is het niet altijd zichtbaar voor betrokkenen wat burgerwetenschap allemaal teweegbrengt. Waag Futurelab onderzocht de handelingsperspectieven (mogelijke acties) die burgerwetenschap biedt voor bewoners, overheden en kennisinstellingen. De publicatie 'Handelingsperspectief dankzij burgerwetenschap' deelt de belangrijkste bevindingen van het onderzoek. Daarbij beschrijft het de waarde van burgerwetenschap, de uitdagingen, en welke stappen er nodig zijn om van inzicht tot verandering te komen.
Op basis van de inzichten van het onderzoek naar handelingsperspectieven is het samenwerkingsspel Aan Zet! ontwikkeld. Aan Zet! helpt om spelenderwijs inzichtelijk te maken welke handelingsperspectieven burgerwetenschap biedt. Het spel is zowel voor gemeenschappen, (lokale) overheden als kennisinstellingen goed toepasbaar om samen in gesprek te gaan over burgerwetenschapsprojecten en een plan op te stellen om daar samen aan te werken.
Wil je meer weten over Aan Zet! of wil je het spel graag spelen? Neem contact met ons op via support [at] hollandse-luchten [dot] org.
Totstandkoming
Het onderzoek naar handelingsperspectieven komt voort uit het burgerwetenschapsproject Hollandse Luchten. Er zijn inzichten uit de meetgroepen van Hollandse Luchten gedocumenteerd en verschillende mensen geïnterviewd. Daarnaast zijn er ook een aantal voorbeelden toegevoegd vanuit andere burgerwetenschapsprojecten. Deze publicatie is in eerste instantie gericht op burgermeetprojecten waarbinnen luchtkwaliteit gemeten wordt met burgerwetenschapssensoren, maar zijn ook breed toepasbaar voor andere burgerwetenschapsprojecten waarin gemeenschappen, (lokale) overheden en kennisinstellingen samenwerken.

title: Chesapeake Bay Blue Crab Numbers See Encouraging Bounceback in New Survey
content:
Conservationists working to turn the tide on declining numbers of blue crabs in the Chesapeake Bay, found some good news in their latest field surveys.
After years of worryingly low numbers, the population appears to be responding to some of the measures implemented to build a crustacean comeback.
This year’s field sampling estimated a total population of 349 million blue crabs in the bay—a 46% increase over last year, according to the annual winter dredge survey.
This raised the population overall to the highest it’s been since 2019, says the report from the Maryland Department of Natural Resources and Virginia Institute of Marine Sciences.
The population of juvenile crabs in winter 2025–26 was estimated to be 228 million, which is also the highest since 2019.
The largest estuary in the US, spanning 200 miles from Maryland to Virginia near Washington DC, the Chesapeake supports more than 3,600 plant and animal species—and the crab remains a cornerstone of the region’s heritage and culture.
In the past 30 years, the surface water temperature of the Chesapeake Bay has increased 1.8 degrees Fahrenheit, but our climate craziness—colder in the winter (which crabs don’t like) and hotter in the summer—isn’t the only cause of the crab conundrum. Human industrialization also plays a role.
MORE GOOD NEWS FROM THE BAY:
• Locally Extinct for a Century, Bay Scallops Thriving Again in Virginia’s Chesapeake
• World’s Largest Oyster Restoration Is Big Success – Fulfilling Virginia’s Promise to Chesapeake Bay Rivers
Also a problem, invasive ‘blue catfish’ are hunting and digging up dormant blue crabs year-round, after having been (stupidly) introduced in the 70s for recreational fishing.
Although recreational and commercial fishing was once a major contributor to falling numbers of blue crabs, the catch limit laws from Maryland and Virginia had solved that issue: separate research from the 2026 Chesapeake Bay Blue Crab Assessment and Advisory report showed no overfishing in the bay.
The numbers can go up and down abruptly, due to many factors, but the neighboring states and federal agencies continue to share data and commit resources to ensure a healthy ecosystem.
And their efforts are paying off. Maryland just released a new report confirming the abundance of underwater sea grasses in the Bay and its tidal tributaries in Maryland last year.
A BAY BEAUTY: Scientists Work to Turn the Tide of Oyster and Seagrass Decline in Chesapeake Bay, Often by Hand
Seagrass coverage—critical for the Bay’s health—expanded from 36,799 acres in 2024 to 41,419 acres in 2025, an increase of nearly 13% in a single year. Bay-wide, acreage reached an estimated 89,385 acres – up 7% from 83,252 acres in 2024.

title: Продолжуваат активностите за маркирање на планинарските патеки на Шар Планина
content:
Продолжуваат активностите за маркирање на планинарските патеки на Шар Планина
- Здружение за Одржлив Развој САТ – Скопје, планинари од Тетово и вработени во Националниот парк од четвртокот, 17 септември продолжија со активностите за поставување и унапредување на планинарската маркација на Шар Планина.
Тетово, 19 септември 2026 (МИА) - Здружение за Одржлив Развој САТ – Скопје, планинари од Тетово и вработени во Националниот парк од четвртокот, 17 септември продолжија со активностите за поставување и унапредување на планинарската маркација на Шар Планина.
Во август од Здружението информираа дека 45 од вкупно 112 новопоставени столбови за зимска маркација на релација Попова Шапка-Титов Врв се уништени, оштетени или отстранети. Таа маркација беше поставувана од ноември 2025 до јуни 2026 година.
„Во рамки на акцијата оваа работна недела беа поставувани патокази и столбови долж Вакафска патека, која претставува летна планинарска патека од Попова Шапка до Титов Врв. Поволните временски услови и обезбедената логистика овозможија паралелно да се собере и транспортира дел од старите прозорци од кулата на Титов Врв, како и дел од уништените столбови од зимската маркација на патеката Попова Шапка – Титов Врв“, соопшти Александар Богоевски од Здружението.
Активностите на терен ќе продолжат и во наредниот период, во зависност од временските услови, со цел подобрување на планинарската инфраструктура и безбедноста на посетителите на Шар Планина пред почетокот на зимата 2026-2027. ас/сст/

title: Mid-Autumn traditions come alive at Ho Chi Minh City art exhibition
content:
The gallery is divided into three spaces inspired by traditional Vietnamese architecture.
At the center is the independent installation Thung Thinh Thung, featuring four northern Vietnamese folk-style lion heads from the Trang Ta traditional toy restoration project suspended above traditional drums.
The lion heads are handcrafted from bamboo and rattan frames, papier-mâché, fabric, and rustic decorative motifs.
Visitors can also listen to a contemporary folk instrumental work composed specifically for the exhibition by artist Dzung.
Other spaces display gouache paintings and works on do paper by renowned painter Nguyen Tu Nghiem, featuring zodiac animals and festivals, alongside a collection of Mid-Autumn-themed woodblock prints.
Through familiar images of lion dances, lantern processions, and full-moon nights, artists from different generations offer new interpretations of folk memories.
Kevin Vuong, the artist behind the Trang Ta project, said his interest in lion dancing began in childhood and later inspired him to recreate the traditional lion.
He said the broader aim is to bring this cultural tradition into everyday life instead of leaving it only in museums or allowing it to be forgotten.
Through the exhibition, Vuong hopes to encourage greater appreciation of Vietnamese folk art.
Tho, co-founder of EMGallery, said the gallery chose the Mid-Autumn Festival theme to create a timely exhibition while helping spread traditional culture more widely in the community.
The exhibition also features an art talk, Folk Art: The Road to Modernity, at 2:30 pm on Saturday, with Kevin Vuong, collector Thanh Uy, contemporary instrumental artist Dzung, and Tho.
A workshop on decorating traditional northern Vietnamese lion heads will take place on Sunday, with sessions from 9:30 am to noon and from 2:30 pm to 5:00 pm. Participants will also hear the Trang Ta team share the story behind the traditional lion-head design.

title: “暮らしやすいまち”の先に脱炭素社会がある。長野県上田市でウェルビーイングとサステナビリティを両立させる「自然エネルギー共同設置推進機構」の挑戦
content:
気候変動を止めよう。
巨大なエネルギーシステムに頼らず生きていこう。
市民の力で自然エネルギーを増やそう。
そんな思いから活動を始めたものの、地域に目を向ければ人口減少を始め、課題は山積み。
エネルギーのシフトに人々が共感する余裕はあるのか？そもそも、このまちに持続可能な未来はあるのだろうか？
そんな問いに端を発し、さまざまな立場の市民が集まって地域の未来を考え直しているのが、長野県上田市を拠点に活動する「一般社団法人自然エネルギー共同設置推進機構（以下、NECO）」です。
2013年の発足から13年間、気候変動の危機を受け、市民のエネルギーシフトを推進するための取り組みを広げてきましたが、人口減少など数々の課題を前に、難しさも感じていました。
新たな展開があったのは2025年。
「地方都市でのウェルビーイングとサステナビリティの両立：逆転と再生（リバース）“一石八鳥”の対話型まちづくりへ」と名付けたプロジェクトが、環境NPO向けに長年助成を行ってきた「地球環境基金」の新たな助成メニュー「戦略プロジェクト（地域協働型）」に採択されたのです。
この助成メニューは、多くの地域が「環境課題が目の前にあっても、そこに取り組む担い手が足りない 」、「過疎化が進んで、高齢者の暮らしを支えることだけで精一杯 」などと悲鳴をあげる現状に対応すべく立ち上げられました。環境問題のみならず複合的な地域課題に向き合い、さまざまな人や組織が協働して持続可能な地域づくりを目指すNGO・NPOの活動を、最大5年間支援します。
NECOは、ここまでどのように歩いてきて、このプロジェクトを通じてどのような未来を描いているのでしょうか。5人のキーパーソンにお話をうかがうために、よくみなさんが作戦会議をする場だという「犀の角」を訪ねました。
「私たちにもできることがある！」3人の出会いからNECOが誕生
最初に上田市で自然エネルギー普及に向けた活動を始めたのは、NPO法人上田市民エネルギー理事長の藤川まゆみさんです。 2005年に上田市に移住した藤川さんは、原発をテーマにした鎌仲ひとみ監督のドキュメンタリー映画『六ヶ所村ラプソディー』をきっかけに自然エネルギーに関心をもつようになり、地域で勉強会の開催を重ねていました。東日本大震災後には、「考えているだけでは、1ワットも生まれない」と、市民発電所の普及を目指すべく、現在のNPO法人を立ち上げます。
そこで生まれたのが、市民による太陽光発電システム「相乗りくん」でした。自宅の屋根を提供する「屋根オーナー」は初期費用・点検費用なしで太陽光パネルを設置し、通常より安い電気代で自然エネルギーを使うことができます。一方、全国各地の「パネルオーナー」は、自宅に屋根がなくても10万円以上の出資をすることで、トータルの売電収入から出資額に応じた還元を得ながら、自然エネルギーの普及に貢献できます。
藤川さん 「相乗りくん」のパネルオーナーになると、自分の出資がどれだけ電気を生み出したかが可視化される。みんなで発電所を訪れるなど、参加者同士で交流もできる。だから「私たちにもできることがある！」とエンパワーされる人がたくさん出てきたんです。
そんな「相乗りくん」のパンフレットを手にして「これ、めちゃくちゃいいアイデアだ！」と声をあげたのが、NECO企画部長の浅輪剛博（あさわ・たかひろ）さんです。
当時、東京に住んでいた浅輪さんも、東日本大震災をきっかけに市民発電の普及を目指すようになり、東京で複数の市民発電所の立ち上げに関わっていました。「相乗りくん」のアイデアに共感した浅輪さんは、何度も上田へ通って上田市民エネルギーの活動を手伝うようになり、自然とその軸足を東京から上田へ移していったといいます。
そして、もう1人。自然エネルギーの研究をしていた信州大学教授の高橋伸英（たかはし・のぶひで）さんも、東日本大震災を機に研究室の外、市井の人たちへ目を向け始めていました。
高橋さん 原発のような巨大な技術に頼っていたら、何かが起きたときに被害を受けるのは市民です。大切なのは、市民自身が「自分たちの暮らしをどう持続可能にしていくのか」という視点を持つこと。机上の空論ではなく、まちに出てみんなと一緒にやっていこう、と僕も思うようになっていきました。
自然エネルギーへの思い、そして「相乗りくん」というアイデアが、3人の出会いをつなぎます。
「相乗りくん」を広めていくためには、法務や税務、発電技術を担う外部組織が必要だと考えた藤川さんは、浅輪さんに相談を持ちかけました。そこで、代表を高橋さんが引き受け、浅輪さんも合流したことで誕生したのが「NECO」だったのです。
脱炭素だけじゃない。まちづくりを起点に「一石八鳥」を目指す
当初、NECOのテーマは「どうすれば市民の手で自然エネルギーを増やせるのか？」でした。しかし、活動を続けるうちに、その問いだけでは太刀打ちできない問題に気づきます。
藤川さん エネルギーをテーマにシンポジウムを開催すれば盛り上がるし、参加した人の意識も変わっていきます。でも、地域に大きな変化が起きるわけではないんですよね。
そんな状況を見て、私たちが言い続けてきた「エネルギーはあらゆる地域課題を解決する」という言葉は口先だけだったのではないか、と気づきました。そのとき、声をかけてくれたのが、千葉商科大学の田中信一郎教授でした。2011年から5年間、長野県庁でエネルギー政策に携わっていた田中さんが 「苦い現実かもしれないけれど、実際、地域にどんな課題があるのか、しっかり見てみましょうよ」と提案してくださったんです。
そこで、2019年に上田市が「第二次上田市総合計画」の後半5年間へ向け「後期まちづくり計画」を策定するにあたり公表されたさまざまなデータを読み込んでみると、人口減少、高齢化、財政難、公共交通の使いにくさ、空き家増加、商店街の衰退、インフラの老朽化、まちが郊外に広がるスプロール化やまちなかが虫食い状態になるスポンジ化など、さまざまな課題が見えてきたのです。そこで気がついたのは、「上田市は持続可能ではない」という現実でした。
エネルギーシフトだけでは地域は変わらない 。そう気づいた3人は、有志による「上田ビジョン研究会」を立ち上げ、「このままでは、上田市は持続可能ではない。みんなで考えていこう」と、さまざまな視点をもつ仲間を集いました。集まったのはNECOや上田市民エネルギーのメンバーに加え、上田市内の建築、福祉、交通、酒造、行政など、まちの未来を真剣に考えるプレイヤーたち。研究会は、上田市の未来を考える集まりを何度も開催しました。
浅輪さん 第1回の集まりは、まさにここ「犀の角」でした。上田市のさまざまな計画書や統計を30〜40冊ずらっと床に並べて、「一人一冊読もう」ということになったんです。
資料を読み、議論を重ねるうちに、思わぬ発見がありました。
まちの課題は、一つひとつが密接につながっていたのです。「それなら、一つの施策で複数の課題を同時に解決できないだろうか？」、「貴重な資源や財源をどこに使えば、同時に複数のメリットを得られるのだろう？」みんなが一石二鳥ならぬ、「一石八鳥」を考え始めました。
たとえば、「公共交通の利便性を上げる」という一つの石を投げれば、「子どもや高齢者の移動のしやすさ」、「交通事故の減少」や「渋滞の解消」、歩く人が増えることで「商店街の活性化」や「健康増進」、駅のそばに住む人が増えることで「まちのコンパクト化」、車の維持費がなくなることで「家庭の支出削減」などが起こる結果、車への依存度も下がり「脱炭素化」にもつながる。一つの施策から複数の効果を生み出すことができ、「一石八鳥」です。
大事なのは一つの仕掛けから多くの効果を得ることで、「脱炭素から入るか、高齢者の移動から入るか」といった順番はさほど重要ではない、ということが次第に明らかになったのです。
藤川さん 「脱炭素を目指しましょう！」と声高に叫ぶより、「暮らしやすいまちを一緒につくりませんか」と語りかけるほうが、たくさんの人が関心をもってくれるとわかってきました。だから、初年度にはあえて「脱炭素」という言葉は使わずにいこう、と思いました。
公共交通を盛り上げる。まちなかに歩きたくなる仕掛けをつくる。既存の建物をシェアしたり、空き家をリノベーションしたりする。農村部と都市部をつなげる。一見バラバラに見える取り組みも、一人ひとりの暮らしを豊かにしながら、その先で脱炭素につながっています。
高橋さん 「環境のために生活を変えてね」と言われても、まちのあり方が変わらなければ、まちの人たちが生活を変えることは難しいです。だから脱炭素を目指すなら、まずはまち全体に目を向けて、さまざまな課題を解決していくことに効果がある。そう気づいて、私たちは「自然エネルギー」から「まちづくり」へと視点をひろげました。
「ウェルビーイングとサステナビリティの両立」に向けた４つのプロジェクト
NECOが先頭に立ち、連携する分野をさらに広げるために始まったのが、2025年の地球環境基金「地域協働型」に採択された「地方都市でのウェルビーイングとサステナビリティの両立：逆転と再生（リバース）“一石八鳥”の対話型まちづくりへ」プロジェクト（以下、「ウェルビーイングとサステナビリティの両立」プロジェクト）。
暮らしやすさや地域の活力を高めることが、地域の人々のウェルビーイングにつながる。そうして変化したライフスタイルが脱炭素やサステナブルな地域へとつながっていく。両方を同時に実現しようというのが、このプロジェクトの目的です。
ここでは、プロジェクトを構成する4つの領域を見てみましょう。
一つ目は「地域共生型のエネルギー事業 」です。
現在、「相乗りくん」は、長野県内で約80か所、合計約1MWを発電中。民家・事業所・公共施設などの屋根を使った太陽光発電に加え、農地に太陽光パネルを設置するソーラーシェアリング（営農型太陽光発電）も広がりつつあります。
浅輪さん 農家さんたちは、この暑さに非常に苦しんでいます。農作物が被害を受けるだけでなく、あまりの暑さで農作業ができないこともあります。だから最近は、農地に日陰をつくるという意味で、ソーラーシェアリングに興味を持つ方が増えているんですよ。暑さという接点で、太陽光発電と農業がつながってきているんですね。
一方、夏に暑く冬は寒い上田市では、「断熱」も欠かせないテーマ。2018年の猛暑をきっかけに、建物の断熱性を高めて冷暖房のエネルギー消費を減らし、CO₂排出量を削減することにも取り組み始めました。
藤川さん 2020年からは、高校生と一緒に教室を断熱するワークショップを始めたんです。生徒たちが「こんなに楽しいんだったら、もっとやりたい」と次年度の計画を自主的につくるようになったり、ワークショップを下級生に引き継ぐ学校が出てきたりしました。長野県は「教室断熱ワークショップのメッカ」と呼ばれるまでになったんですよ。
「楽しいから、もっとやってみたい！」。そんな言葉からは、生徒たちが環境活動を「楽しみながら、日々をより快適にするもの」と捉えていることが伝わってきます。
2つ目は「交通まちづくり」です。
空き家や空き店舗が増え、徒歩圏内で買い物などを済ませることが難しくなり、多くの人が車に頼るようになった上田市。そこで考えたのが、地域の足である上田電鉄・別所線の利用者を増やすための働きかけ。読んだら乗りたくなる新聞「しおだトッコトコ」を発行したり、答えると乗りたくなるアンケート調査を実施したり、1,000円で5,500円分利用できる「別所線エコチケ」を試験的に販売したりしました。
鉄道利用者が増えれば駅の近くに人が集まり、商店街の活性化や地価・税収のアップにもつながる。歩く機会が増えれば人は健康になり、脱車社会は脱炭素社会につながっていく。まさに「一石八鳥」の試みです。
2023年11月、上田市は「第4回環境省脱炭素先行地域」に採択されました。地域で生み出した再生可能エネルギーで別所線を支えるという仕組みを含め、NECOが提唱してきた「交通まちづくり」という考え方が共感を呼んだ結果だ、とみなさんは胸を張ります。
2025年12月に販売した「別所線エコチケ」は、わずか2日で1,000枚が完売。購入者の約7割は「普段は別所線を利用しない人」だったといいます。鉄道事業者の上田電鉄も挑戦を続けています。同年3月、上田電鉄は平日の運行本数を56便から78便に増便しました。さらに、駅周辺でシェアサイクルの整備なども進め、別所線の利用者は7％増加（前年度比）。
2025年からNECOの活動に加わった企画部の栗本京子（くりもと・きょうこ）さんは、別所線の利用促進に取り組んでいます。
栗本さん 私たちは、「絶対に電車を使ってくださいね！」と言っているわけではありません。別所線は2両編成。みんなが乗ると、都心みたいな満員電車になってしまいます（笑）。いま車を利用している人のうち、ごく一部が電車に変えるだけで十分インパクトがあります。
3つ目のキーワードは、「城下町エリアビジョン」です。
上田城跡公園にはたくさんの観光客が訪れますが、そこから約1.5km圏内に位置する上田駅前を含む城下町エリアまで足を延ばす人は多くありません。どうすれば、まちなかに人の流れをつくれるのか。そんな課題意識から、上田市と「上田ビジョン研究会」がパートナーシップ協定を結び、多様な市民と協働しながら「上田城 城下町エリアビジョン」の策定に向けて動き出しました。
上田市役所でエリアビジョンの策定を担当するのは、上田市都市建設部・都市計画課・調査計画担当の倉根明徳（くらね・あきのり）さんです。
倉根さん 行政がまちのビジョンをつくるときは、コンサルタントに委託して案をつくり、最後にパブリックコメントを募集して仕上げていくのが一般的です。でも、それだと多くの市民は置いていかれたように感じてしまうし、行政だけで進めると、方向を間違えてしまうかもしれない。だから、今回のエリアビジョン策定にあたり、上田市に住む人たちと一緒に進めるべきだ、と最初から思っていました。
エリアビジョン策定へ向け、市内に通う高校生約400人へのアンケートも含め、多くの市民に投げかけたのは「この城下町がどうなったら、あなたはハッピーですか？」というシンプルな問いでした。集まったのは、「休憩できる木陰やベンチがほしい」、「商店街を歩行者天国に」、「歩きたくなるようなマップがほしい」など率直な声。現在は、それぞれの実現性を模索しつつ、裏通りでのマルシェイベント「261（にーろく市）」の支援や、解体工事が進む旧市民会館から受け継いだ廃材でつくったベンチの設置なども実践しています。
倉根さん 僕たちは「歩いてください！」と言いたいわけではないんです。「歩くと楽しいし、健康になれるから、週1回ぐらい歩いてみようかな」と思ってもらえたらうれしい。楽しくやっていけるのが一番なんですよ。
歩くことが、健康や人との出会いを生み出すと同時に、車への依存を減らし、脱炭素にもつながる。まさに、ウェルビーイングとサステナビリティを同時に実現する取り組みです。
4つ目は、今後注力していきたい「農村・森林」の領域です。
先ほどご紹介したソーラーシェアリングも、そうした取り組みの一つ。
さらには、「どうすれば農山村の集落と自然のエコシステムと、そこでのウェルビーイングな暮らしを維持できるのか」という視点から、NECOは新たに農山村とまちなかをつなぐ地域づくりにも着手しようとしています。
浅輪さん 上田市のような地方都市の強みは、農山村と都市部が近くにあること。それぞれの特色を活かして連携しあえば、地域の価値を大きく上げることができます。
すでに、上田市近郊では、珍しい野菜の栽培に着手したり、ブドウをワインに、お米を日本酒に加工したり、棚田をマーケティングして都会とつなげたりと、地域資源に付加価値をつけ、農家の収益性を高める動きも始まりました。今後は、農村集落とデザイナー、IT、金融、エネルギー事業者、加工・販売業者をつなぐマッチングや、兼業農家がゲストハウスを運営する仕組みづくりなど、農山村で仕事と暮らしの選択肢を広げる取り組みも本格的に始めるそうです。
上田リバース会議――まちを変える「対話」を生む場
「ウェルビーイングとサステナビリティの両立」プロジェクトが、地域のさまざまなステイクホルダーとともに展開できるのは、その土台となる関係性があるからです。ここで、少し時間を巻き戻してみましょう。
2021年、さまざまな地域課題を前に「このままでは上田市は持続できない」と危機感を抱いた上田ビジョン研究会は、主催する集まりに「上田リバース会議」という名前をつけました。
人口減少や空き家の増加など、地域の課題が深刻化していく流れを逆転（reverse）させ、上田を再生（rebirth）させていく。そんな思いを込めています。
浅輪さん 「リバース」という言葉には、拡大を前提としてきた社会のあり方を見直そうという思いも込めています。まちを拡大するときには協力できても、縮小させようとすると、新たな難しさが生じやすいですよね。これまで流れていた方向を逆転させるということですから。だからこそ、お互いの立場を越えて、みんなでまちのビジョンを描く場が必要だったんです。
上田リバース会議は年に6〜7回開かれ、企業関係者、商店主、農家、行政職員、研究者、子育て世代、学生など、オンラインも組み合わせると、1回に平均100人程度が集まります。
会議の流れは、試行錯誤を繰り返しながら定めていきました。
まずはその日のテーマについて、上田市の地域のデータを全員で共有し、前提を踏まえて参加者の目線がそろったところで、その分野の第一人者（ゲスト講師）から最新の知見を学びます。少人数のグループに分かれて対話をし、後半にはスマートフォンのフォームで質問を集め、それを画面で一緒に見ながらゲストとディスカッションします。
藤川さん 最初はみんなで輪になって話し合っていました。でも、それだと「討論」になってしまったり、声の大きい人だけが発言して終わってしまったりする。それで、少人数のグループで対話をするような形に変えていきました。３〜４人が一番話しやすいと思います。
主催者としては、その日のゴールを思い描いていますが、そこへ誘導することはしません。対話を重ねるなかで、一人ひとりが「目指す方向はこっちだね」と納得していく。そのプロセスを何より大切にしているのです。
全員の意見を無理に一つにまとめることもしません。ゆるやかな方向性を共有しながら、それぞれの違いも認めていく。そんな「ゆるさ」も、この会議の特徴です。
「行政vs市民」から、ともに考える関係へ
こうした進め方を大切にしているのは、市民と行政が安心して同じテーブルにつくためでもありました。
藤川さんは、1回目の上田リバース会議を開く前、「行政職員にも参加してほしい」と上田市役所を訪ねました。そのときに返ってきた言葉が忘れられないと言います。
藤川さん 担当の方から、「僕らは、そういう場で吊し上げを食らうのはつらいんだよね」と言われたんです。たしかに、住民説明会のような場で市民が行政を追及する光景は珍しくありません。私自身も「どうしてできないんですか！」と詰め寄ったことがあります。
だからこそ、「行政を責める場」ではなく「一緒に考える場」をつくりたい。そう思ったことが、上田リバース会議の原点ですね。
行政職員は立場上、個人の考えを口に出せないことも多々あります。その“鎧”を安心して少し脱げるような会、行政職員も含め参加者全員がエンパワメントされるような会。それがみなさんが描く理想でした。
藤川さん 行政だけでもできないし、市民だけでもできない。だから行政と市民でタッグを組みたい。そのためには、どうやって信頼関係をつくっていけばいいんだろう？そう考えていくなかで、データで目線を合わせ、一緒に学び、対話する上田リバース会議なら、行政と市民がともにエンパワメントされると気づきました。
回を重ねるごとに、行政側にも変化が生まれました。ある回の終了後には、参加した行政職員から「これは市長をはじめ、職員全員で聞くべき話でした！」という声があがったといいます。
上田リバース会議は単なる勉強会でも、意見交換会でもありません。
藤川さん曰く、まちに変化を起こすための「仕掛け」。倉根さん曰く、異なる課題をもつ人たちが同じゴールにたどりつくための「入口」。表現は人それぞれですが、込められた思いは同じです。
倉根さん リバース会議は行政と市民がお互いの立場を理解しながら一緒に考える場なので、僕たちも安心して参加できるんですよ。しかも、楽しい。僕にとっては、それが原動力ですね。
地球環境基金が後押しする「次の一歩」
2025年度以降へ向け、NECOがこれまで取り組んできた「ウェルビーイングとサステナビリティの両立」プロジェクトの次なる展開を描き、地球環境基金の新規助成メニュー「地域協働型」に応募したのは、公共交通を軸にしたまちづくりや、これから力を入れていきたい農山村との連携事業を、本格的に動かすためでした。
というのも、NECOにとって太陽光発電は収益化が進んでいる一方、公共交通や農村・森林の領域では収益を生み出しにくく、それらを支える活動も寄付やボランティアに頼らざるを得ない状況だったからです。
浅輪さん 僕たちは、環境にまつわる仕事できちっと食べていける社会をつくりたいと思っています。学校でSDGsを学んで、「環境問題に関わる仕事がしたい」と思っている若者はたくさんいます。でも、それを仕事に結びつける道筋がまだ少ないんですよ。地球環境基金の「地域協働型」メニューでは、助成金の上限50％を人件費に充てることができます。うまく活用していきたいですね。
実際に、今回の助成によって、新たに栗本さんが仲間に加わりました。今後は助成金に頼らずフルタイムワーカーを増やすことも、目標の一つです。
今回の助成メニュー「地域協働型」の理念には、地域で多主体が協働して取り組むことに加え、「地域活動で得たノウハウを他地域へ展開していくこと」も含まれています。NECOはさまざまな課題に関する知見を積み上げてきましたが、他地域へ広げたいのは個々の事業そのものよりも、みんなでつくり上げてきた立場の垣根を越えて協働を促す「上田リバース会議」の組み立て方だといいます。
現在、栗本さんと藤川さんを中心に、そのノウハウをまとめた「リバースマニュアル」の制作が進められています。
栗本さん たとえば講演会を開催しても、「いい講演だったね」で終わってしまうことが多いですよね。でも、まちを変えたいという目的があって開催したのだから、具体的な変化につなげたい。そんな思いを持っている人たちに、このマニュアルが届いたらうれしいですね。
「リバースマニュアル」のうち「会のつくり方」は、すでにホームページ上で公開されていますが、栗本さんたちは現在、より充実した内容を冊子としてまとめ、より多くの人の手に届けるべく奮闘中。2026年度内には完全版の完成を目指しているといいます。
当たり前の日々を未来へ
こうした一つひとつの取り組みを重ねるなかで、NECOという組織が目指していく姿、そしてそれぞれの事業にかける思いも、少しずつ変わってきました。今となっては、みなさんが願うのは「まちの持続」そのものです。
高橋さん NECOを立ち上げた頃は、地域エネルギー会社のような存在になれたらと思っていました。でもいまや、僕たちは、エネルギーを入り口にした“まちづくり会社”のようなかたちになっています。最終的には、こうした活動で助成金に頼らず自走していけたらいいですよね。
そんな高橋さんの言葉を、藤川さんが力強く受け取りました。
藤川さん 私にもできることがあってよかった！、と思うんです。まちづくりのためなら何かできることがある。10代から高齢の方まで、「これ、おもしろいからやろう！」と思える人が増えたらいいですよね。「私たち、もっとできるよね」って、お互いにエンパワーできる社会が理想です。
なぜ、まちのためにこんなにがんばれるのでしょう？
最後に、そう問いかけてみました。
浅輪さん 「犀の角」と「上田映劇」がずっと残っていてほしいからかな。これからも、このまちで演劇とか映画を楽しみたいな、と思うんですよ。
一見、個人的な願いに聞こえるかもしれません。
けれども、その願いを支えるのは、自然エネルギー、脱炭素、人の流れ、まちの経済、公共交通など、さまざまな要素がつながり、まちそのものが多角的に変わっていくことです。
公共交通が使いやすくなれば、車を使わずに歩く人が増え、二酸化炭素排出が減り、駅の近くに人が集まる。
まちなかに人の流れが生まれれば、商店街が活性化し、地域経済も動き出す。
そうしてまちが持続すれば、誰もが日々の暮らしを楽しみ続けることができる。
同じように、みんなで自然エネルギーをつくれば、新たな人のつながりやお金の循環が生まれ、地域の活力が育まれていく。そして、そうした循環は地域の暮らしをより豊かなものにしながら、気候変動という地球規模の課題解決にもつながっていく。
暮らしやすいまちをつくることと、地球環境を守ることは、別々の目標ではありません。
それこそが、「ウェルビーイングとサステナビリティの両立」なのです。
（撮影：山田智大）

「地球環境基金「戦略プロジェクト（地域協働型）」は、環境NPOや団体が行政・企業・市民など異なるセクターと協働しながら、地域課題の解決に取り組むプロジェクトを支援する助成制度です。
2027年度助成金募集については、地球環境基金のホームページにて募集内容を公開しています。
地球環境基金「戦略プロジェクト（地域協働型）」の採択団体が登壇し、地域協働で取り組む環境課題解決をテーマにしたイベントを開催します。
脱炭素・まちづくり・生物多様性・流域保全など、それぞれ異なるフィールドで、行政・企業・市民と協働してきたプロセスと手応えと地域協働のヒントを、具体的なエピソードとともにお伝えします。

title: Baby bank helping more parents in full-time work
content:
Baby bank helping more parents in full-time work
- Published
A Birmingham baby bank says it is helping a growing number of people in full-time work who are struggling to afford essentials for their children.
Kavita Kaur Dhillon and her husband Karvinder run the Handsworth Baby and Family Bank on Soho Road, which provides free items including nappies, baby formula, clothes and toys.
The couple said the majority of people they first helped were from low-income households, but they were now seeing more working families needing support with everyday costs.
"We don't need any more clothing, it's the everyday essentials, formula, nappies, wipes, toiletries," said Kavita.
Karvinder said demand had shifted in recent years.
"Before, we mainly needed nappies," he said.
"As the daily cost of living has gone up, people need help with more day-to-day things."
The couple said they were currently in desperate need of baby formula and often had only a handful of tubs left in stock.
"Just because you dress nice, or drive a nice car, doesn't mean you don't need help," Kavita said.
"Nobody knows people's circumstances. People can judge, but the reality is people are struggling."
The bank, which operates from inside the couple's Dhillons Boutique store, has been helping families since 2024.
Kavita believed sharing a space with the shop helped remove some of the stigma that can come with asking for support.
"You go out of our shop and people think you have purchased something, but in fact you've just used our baby bank," she said.
She described it as a "warm and welcoming space" and said demand had continued to grow since it opened.
For the couple, supporting families remains the most rewarding part of the project.
"For me it is fulfilling, knowing I've been able to support or help someone else be okay and smile," Kavita said.
She urged anyone who was struggling not to suffer in silence.
"It's nothing to be ashamed of or to be scared of. There's no shame in asking for help."

title: Local leaders have say on reforms to prepare youngsters for work
content:
Local leaders have say on reforms to prepare youngsters for work
Education Secretary convenes leaders from education, industry, and local government at No.10 North to put local expertise at heart of education policies.
Local leaders are to have their say on how to drive excellence across the education system and better prepare young people for work during a summit hosted by the Education Secretary.
Regional mayors, business leaders, headteachers and college principals will convene today (10 September 2026) at No.10 North in Manchester to shape plans to make England a technical education superpower, and ensure technical and academic education are on an equal footing.
It comes following the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) international education rankings earlier in the week – which showed England improved or remained stable against an international backdrop of declining scores and continues to perform significantly above the OECD averages in all 3 subjects. Meanwhile, Estonia shows academic and technical excellence can coexist.
Discussions will focus on the delivery of vocational education reforms from aged 14, work experience opportunities, and making the most of the devolution of billions of pounds of funding for 16 to 19-year-olds.
The meeting will be the first of regular gatherings that will bring together industry, politicians and educators to drive forward reforms. It comes ahead of the publication of the Devolution white paper which will set out plans to give local leaders a greater role in shaping economic growth and opportunity in their areas.
Education Secretary Lucy Powell is set to say in her opening remarks:
I want a new way of working in education. I want change to come not from Whitehall alone, but to be co-designed with those who will deliver it, those who know local strengths and challenges best – you and your colleagues.
That’s what we’re here today, and that’s how I want us to see devolution. I want it to be at the heart of a different way of doing things: a partnership between national government and local areas, so that we can bring the change that children, young people and families need, up and down the country.
The reforms build on the government introducing V levels from aged 16 and expanding T levels from next September to help to tackle the nearly 1 million young people who are not in education, employment or training.
On the same day, Minister Smith will use her first address to the higher education sector at the start of the new term to call on universities to see themselves at the heart of this reform agenda, helping bring growth to every postcode.
Speaking at University UK’s annual conference, she will urge the sector to work with local leaders, colleges, and employers to identify opportunities locally to shape courses and create work experience.
In her speech to university heads, Minister Smith is set to say:
There’s no point building the growth this country desperately needs, if it just embellishes the places that are already prosperous. Growth should spread opportunity and prosperity widely, leaving no area behind.
This vision for widespread growth makes universities’ local connections and contributions just as important as their national and international renown.
Your institutions are a network of economic engines throughout the country. We want to build on your established strengths and successes to distribute opportunity and drive national renewal.
Universities should be at the heart of local partnerships that turn economic opportunity into courses, student workplace experience and good jobs for local people.
This is already happening in areas such as the Humber where the University of Hull works with major local employers including wind turbine manufacturer Siemens Gamesa and renewable energy developer Ørsted. Students can access placements and graduate opportunities, while a master’s degree apprenticeship developed with Siemens Gamesa is training the next generation of offshore wind engineers.
Meanwhile, in the West of England, UWE Bristol and University Centre Weston work with employers including Airbus, Rolls-Royce and GKN Aerospace to deliver engineering degree apprenticeships. Learners combine paid work with degree-level study, while employers help shape training around the skills needed in aerospace and advanced manufacturing.
Chief Executive of the Sixth Form Colleges Association, Bill Watkin, said:
Today’s summit is a very welcome opportunity to discuss how to implement the ambitious reforms set out by the new Prime Minister and Secretary of State.
We share the government’s ambition to reduce the number of young people not in education, employment and training - this is an important national priority that we must all come together to address.
Today could mark the beginning of a new chapter in collaboration between education, industry and government to ensure that every young person can access a high quality pathway to skilled employment or further study.
Chief Executive of the Association of Colleges, David Hughes, said:
The Prime Minister’s has set out a clear and exciting vision of positive pathways for young people through technical education into good jobs from age 14. Those pathways need to go all the way to the highest levels of learning and to open up great careers.
Colleges already contribute so much in this area, and the roundtable is a great opportunity to build the local partnerships needed to scale that work up, with elected mayor’s leading. I’m pleased that the Education Secretary is bringing us all together, there’s a lot to win and a lot to plan for.
Chief Executive of the Confederation of School Trusts, Leora Cruddas CBE said:
I am pleased to be attending this important summit. Public institutions should be understood not simply as mechanisms for delivering services, but as enduring civic assets that generate belonging, trust, and democratic legitimacy.
The strength of a nation depends on the vitality of its local institutions and the relationships between and among them. School trusts in England are civic institutions alongside further education colleges, universities, and NHS trusts, with the capacity to support civic leadership in place.
Amazon UK Country Manager, John Boumphrey, said:
Talent is evenly distributed across this country, but opportunity is not.
At Amazon, around half the people who join our operations teams come either from unemployment or straight from education - including from communities where opportunity is hardest to find.
When you give young people the right support, they thrive. It’s as simple as that. We’re proud to be helping every young person see a real route into a career.

title: 沉浸式科普点亮青少年"爱农强农"植保梦
content: 时值九月，序属三秋，天高云淡，金风送爽。为践行人与自然和谐共生理念，厚植青少年爱农知农强农情怀，2026年9月19日，中国农业科学院植物保护研究所以"新植保赋能生态治理，全健康护航粮食安全"为主题，面向社会公众开展沉浸式科普教育，举办第八届农科开放日专场科普活动。 观测农药非靶标生物。 来自人大附中西山学校、中国农大附小、中关村第一小学等数十所学校的中小学生，在家长陪同下走进植保所院区，奔赴植保知识小课堂、科研实践微体验、趣味互动小游戏三大主题活动板块。据植保所李宁博士介绍，活动坚持科普为民，统筹知识性、趣味性、体验感，把实验室前沿科研成果转化为通俗易懂、可感可参与的科普内容，推动高端科研资源向社会科普资源转化。 观察啮齿动物头骨标本。 植保知识小课堂内，科研人员紧扣社会关注热点开展专题科普宣讲。陈景超博士以"给生态留点'鼠'空间"为题，介绍草原鼠害科学防控理念，破除"灭鼠就要赶尽杀绝"的片面认知。人大附中西山学校学生梁以沫说："通过'三分钟识别外来入侵物种'科普，我认识了加拿大一枝黄花等危险入侵生物。"活动面向青少年及家长普及农业生物安全知识，引导全社会树牢生物安全风险防范意识，夯实农业生物安全的群众基础。 动手体验豇豆农药残留快速检测。 科研实践微体验区向参观者开放农作物、杂草、啮齿动物、各类昆虫标本资源。"小小农残侦探"体验点位上，同学们动手操作农残检测试纸，完整体验农产品质量安全检测流程；现场演示病毒检测试剂盒实操实验，把实验室科研场景搬到科普一线；张浩文博士依托昆虫雷达科普展台，深入浅出讲解虫情监测预警技术原理；黄红娟博士借助寄生植物列当科普展板，生动讲述农田生态中奇妙的植物攻防关系。 孩子们参加寻宝大作战活动，找寻白星花金龟幼虫。 趣味游戏互动区设置了丰富的互动项目。孩子们在闯关游戏中区分益虫与害虫，学习昆虫生物学特性、生物防治等专业知识，实现寓教于乐。一位学生家长表示，这类科普跳出课本局限，让孩子看得见、摸得着，真正读懂保障国家粮食安全、维护生态保护的时代意义。 杂草鼠害与草地有害生物防控中心主任刘晓辉研究员表示，新时代植物保护工作，要摒弃简单灭杀的传统思路，牢固树立生命共同体理念，综合运用生态调控、绿色防控技术，统筹农业生产发展与生物多样性保护，践行人与自然和谐共生的"全健康"理念，以科技创新守护粮食安全与生态安全。 植保所副所长陈捷胤表示，用好农科开放日平台，开展好科普服务，是科研"国家队"履行社会责任的重要实践，帮助青少年厚植热爱农科、敬畏自然的理想种子，为培育知农爱农时代新人积蓄力量。植保所纪委书记刘水长表示，植保所将发挥国家级科研院所科普示范作用，不断丰富科普载体、创新科普形式，面向社会大众普及植物保护、农业生物安全相关知识，助力提升全民科学素养。 活动由植保所党委办公室、杂草鼠害与草地有害生物防控中心承办，累计吸引600余个家庭、近2000名群众参与。 （本文图片均由中国农科院植保所提供）

title: Pitch perfect cultural diplomacy wins heart of China’s first lady Peng Liyuan
content:
Pitch perfect cultural diplomacy wins heart of China’s first lady Peng Liyuan
Young singers’ rendition of beloved folk song ‘Jasmine Flower’ evokes warm reaction from the renowned soprano during Smithsonian visit
Footage shows the Hope Chinese School youth choir waving Chinese and American national flags during their rendition of the song “Jasmine Flower”, while Peng watches with a smile, her lips moving along to the lyrics.
As the performance ends, she turns to her US counterpart and smiles, while placing a hand to her heart, visibly moved. The two first ladies applaud the children, with Peng calling out “bravo”.
The iconic Chinese folk song, also known as “Mo Li Hua”, has long been part of Peng’s repertoire.
As a celebrated soprano with the People’s Liberation Army, she has sung it on numerous major occasions, including the 2008 Beijing Olympics one-year countdown celebration at Tiananmen Square.

title: Solad Accelerates Solar Home System Deployment
content:
Latest Headlines
Solad Accelerates Solar Home System Deployment
Kayode Tokede
Solad is accelerating access to Solar Home Systems across underserved communities in Nigeria as the country enters a new phase in the growth of distributed renewable energy.
Solad has already deployed more than 1,800 Solar Home Systems across five Nigerian states, with a further 4,000 plus earmarked for roll-out.
The programme expands the company’s distributed energy footprint and supports Nigeria’s ambition to widen reliable electricity access. The programme forms part of Solad’s broader strategy of delivering decentralised energy at multiple levels; from individual homes and micro-enterprises through to market-scale mini-grids and commercial and industrial solar installations.
Solad’s Solar Home Systems programme is being implemented within the rapidly expanding ecosystem created by the Rural Electrification Agency and the World Bank-supported Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Scale-Up (DARES) programme.
DARES represents one of Africa’s most ambitious programmes of its kind and is designed to accelerate renewable electricity access through both solar-hybrid mini-grids and standalone solar systems.
For Solad, the significance of the programme extends beyond the number of systems installed: each connection can support real economic activity. Solar electricity allows a small retailer to remain open longer, a tailor to operate electrical equipment without relying on a petrol generator, a household to power lighting and communication equipment, and a micro-enterprise to redirect money previously spent on fuel towards growing the business.
The Chief Executive of Solad’s Nigerian businesses, Yewande Olagbende, in a statement said: “Nigeria’s energy-access challenge cannot be solved by a single technology or a single type of infrastructure. We need solutions at every level; from large power infrastructure to mini-grids and individual solar systems.
“Solar Home Systems are particularly important because they can be deployed quickly and directly into communities where conventional grid expansion may take many years to arrive.
“For Solad, this is fundamentally about economic empowerment. When reliable electricity reaches a home or small business, the impact goes far beyond keeping the lights on. It creates additional working hours, reduces dependence on expensive generators, and gives entrepreneurs a more reliable foundation on which to build their businesses.”
Solad’s latest deployment builds on a long-standing involvement in Nigeria’s distributed energy sector. The Company has developed and operated energy infrastructure serving businesses and communities across Nigeria and has previously participated in programmes administered by the Rural Electrification Agency under the Nigeria Electrification Project. Solad’s portfolio today spans Solar Home Systems, mini-grids, commercial and industrial solar, battery storage, and decentralised energy infrastructure.
The company’s experience demonstrates the increasingly vital role indigenous private-sector developers can play in translating national energy-access policy and development finance into operating infrastructure on the ground.
Beyond expanding access to electricity, Solad presents its Solar Home Systems programme as a platform for local enterprise growth, job creation, and long-term customer support.
Nigeria’s renewable energy market is entering a period of significant expansion, with large-scale programmes supported by the federal government, Rural Electrification Agency, World Bank Group, and other development finance institutions combining public-sector support with private-sector execution and capital.
That combination is helping to shift the sector from individual renewable energy projects towards a more scalable distributed energy industry.
Solad said it believes that three elements will be critical to that transition: deployment at scale, strong local operating capability, and reliable long-term customer support. This is why the company’s investment extends beyond equipment.
Solad is building teams of technicians, sales and customer-support personnel capable of operating across the communities in which its systems are installed. The company recently brought together members of its DARES technical and customer-service teams for dedicated training focused on after-sales service and maintenance of deployed Solar Home Systems.
Constantine ‘Labi Ogunbiyi, the chairman and co-founder of Solad Power Group, said: “Africa’s energy transition will ultimately be judged by what gets built and by the economic activity that infrastructure enables.
“The opportunity presented by programmes such as DARES is to combine public policy, development capital and private-sector execution to build a genuinely scalable decentralised energy market.
“Solad has been working in this market for several years. Our focus now is execution; deploying more systems, expanding our operating footprint and demonstrating that African renewable energy businesses can build commercially sustainable platforms while delivering meaningful social and economic impact.”
On the Solad’s rollout, the Head of the Nigeria Electrification Programme (NEP) at the Rural Electrification Agency (REA), Femi Akinyelure, said: “The DARES programme is designed to significantly expand access to reliable and sustainable electricity by creating the conditions for distributed renewable energy solutions to be deployed at scale. A central part of this approach is enabling capable private-sector providers to extend standalone solar and mini-grid solutions to underserved households, businesses and communities across Nigeria.
“Through DARES, we are building on the experience and lessons of the Nigeria Electrification Project to move from individual interventions towards a larger, more sustainable market for distributed renewable energy. Our focus is not only on the number of connections delivered, but on ensuring that expanded electricity access supports livelihoods, productive economic activity and improved quality of life for Nigerians.”
Solar Home Systems form one component of Solad’s wider clean energy strategy. The group is developing and operating solutions across the energy spectrum, ranging from household and MSME systems to market-scale renewable energy infrastructure and commercial and industrial installations. Solad has deployed approximately 6.2 MW of clean and renewable energy capacity, and its operational footprint includes projects serving businesses and communities as well as commercial and industrial customers.
The company sees significant opportunity in connecting these different segments into a broader distributed energy platform capable of providing reliable power wherever conventional electricity supply remains inadequate. Building on its existing Solar Home System rollout, Solad intends to continue expanding that platform while investing in the people, technology and operating infrastructure required to support customers over the long term.
Olagbende added: “The next stage of Nigeria’s renewable energy story is about scale. We have demonstrated that the technology works. We now need to demonstrate that we can build the distribution, financing, technical and customer-service infrastructure required to reach millions more people. That is the opportunity Solad is positioning itself to address.”

title: Curta pernambucano ‘Guél Boy’ circula por Recife e Olinda com quatro sessões gratuitas
content:
O curta-metragem pernambucano “Guél Boy”, dirigido por Ayla Òbì, realiza quatro exibições gratuitas entre esta quinta-feira (17) e domingo (20), sempre às 19 horas, em diferentes territórios do Recife e de Olinda. A circulação começou na quarta-feira (16), no Centro Cultural Periférico Aurora Candidé, em Olinda, e segue nesta quinta no Coque, na sexta-feira (18) na Ilha de Deus e no sábado (19) no Recife Antigo. As sessões são acompanhadas de bate-papos com integrantes da equipe e contam com interpretação em Libras.
Produzido a partir de uma perspectiva ligada à cultura periférica, “Guél Boy” acompanha quatro jovens negros do Recife, Uilson, Marlon, Duda e Ninha, interpretados por Gabriel Oliveira, Haryson Ribeiro, Rayssa Canuto e Kamile Nascimento. A narrativa parte das relações de amizade entre os personagens para abordar os efeitos do racismo estrutural e as formas encontradas pela juventude negra para construir seus próprios espaços de afeto, expressão e pertencimento.
A história se desenvolve em meio ao cotidiano da cidade, atravessado por manifestações culturais como o passinho do bregafunk, o grafite, a pichação, a poesia e a produção musical. As redes sociais e os jogos online também aparecem como elementos que fazem parte da experiência dos personagens e ajudam a compor um retrato da juventude negra contemporânea.
A obra utiliza ainda recursos do realismo fantástico para criar uma abordagem própria sobre as experiências vividas pelos jovens. Toda a produção foi gravada com celular e drone, explorando cores, luminosidade e paisagens associadas ao verão recifense. A direção de fotografia é de Roberto Iuri, enquanto Rose Lima e Júlia Machado assinam a produção.
A relação entre racismo e representação também está no centro do filme. A narrativa questiona a maneira como programas policiais e meios de comunicação hegemônicos podem contribuir para a criminalização da juventude negra, contrapondo essa perspectiva às experiências de amizade, criatividade e convivência construídas pelos personagens.
O elenco reúne artistas com trajetórias ligadas à cultura periférica e ao audiovisual. Entre eles estão Okado do Canal, que já participou de curtas e de um longa-metragem, e Samuel Mucão, também com atuação no audiovisual.
Para a diretora Ayla Òbì, a amizade e a vida em comunidade são elementos fundamentais da história. Segundo ela, o filme busca apresentar outras possibilidades de existência diante das representações produzidas pelo racismo.
“Apesar da imposição e atravessamento de distorções que se originam do racismo estrutural do Brasil através da mídia e da segurança pública, no filme, as pessoas vivem suas vidas organizando momentos que contradizem essa lógica da branquitude. Sendo assim, é um filme que, em seu gesto, por si só, é uma homenagem à vida e à cultura periférica”, afirma.
Parte dos locais escolhidos para a circulação também integra os espaços onde o curta foi filmado. A proposta é aproximar a obra dos territórios e das comunidades que dialogam com sua narrativa, além de criar momentos de conversa sobre cinema negro, audiovisual periférico e as experiências presentes no filme.
Todas as exibições têm acessibilidade comunicacional com interpretação em Libras e entrada gratuita.
O projeto conta com apoio da Secretaria de Cultura de Pernambuco, por meio de recursos da Política Nacional Aldir Blanc de Fomento à Cultura (PNAB), do Ministério da Cultura e do Governo Federal.

title: Bewoners van nieuw asielcentrum in Ukkel maken fietstocht om buurt te leren kennen
content:
Tegen het asielcentrum in de Ukkelse Beeckmanstraat kwam heel wat protest. Fietsorganisatie Uccle Avello wil in samenwerking met Samusocial (de uitbater van het centrum) de nieuwe bewoners nu toch op een leuke manier laten kennismaken met de buurt.
Bewoners van nieuw asielcentrum in Ukkel maken fietstocht om buurt te leren kennen
Sinds 15 september komen de eerste asielzoekers aan in het opvangcentrum in Ukkel. Het gaat voornamelijk om gezinnen met kinderen, in totaal zo'n 230 mensen.
Middels een fietstocht willen Samusocial, Uccle Avello en vzw Du haut de mon potager hen leren kennismaken met de buurt op Autoloze Zondag. Er zijn drie fietstochten gepland: om 14 uur, 15.30 uur en 17 uur.
Groepjes van vijf tot acht bewoners worden begeleid door gidsen en maken kennis met verschillende nuttige plekken: scholen, bibliotheken, winkels, parken en het openbaar vervoer. De route loopt onder meer langs het Wolvendaalpark, het Raspailpark en het Heldenplein, zodat de deelnemers vertrouwd kunnen raken met hun nieuwe omgeving. Later zullen er nog cursussen worden georganiseerd voor diegenen die hun fietsvaardigheid in het stadsverkeer willen verbeteren.

title: Alberi per trattenere l’azoto e tecniche di semina intelligenti: così gli agricoltori della Tanzania si stanno adattando alle precipitazioni imprevedibili
content:
Alberi per trattenere l’azoto e tecniche di semina intelligenti: così gli agricoltori della Tanzania si stanno adattando alle precipitazioni imprevedibili
Indice
A Udumka la risposta alle piogge che arrivano male, troppo forti o tutte insieme sta crescendo dentro un vivaio. La comunità del sud della Tanzania ha cominciato a coltivare specie capaci di trattenere acqua e fissare l’azoto, inserendole in terreni messi alla prova dalle coltivazioni intensive e dalle precipitazioni che possono trascinare via i nutrienti. Nessuna tecnologia futuriatica. Qui si piantano alberi.
Il vivaio è gestito dall’Udumka Environmental Group, collettivo locale coinvolto nel progetto Her Resilience, Our Planet. La scelta delle specie serve a recuperare gradualmente fertilità e a rendere i campi meno fragili davanti a un clima diventato più irregolare. A lavorarci ci sono anche formatori scelti e preparati all’interno della comunità, così le conoscenze non rimangono appese all’arrivo di tecnici esterni. È uno degli interventi raccontati da CARE Tanzania, che partecipa al progetto.
Gli alberi entrano nei campi
Gli alberi azotofissatori lavorano soprattutto sottoterra. Grazie alla relazione con alcuni batteri presenti nelle radici, contribuiscono a rendere disponibile nel sistema agricolo l’azoto atmosferico, uno dei nutrienti essenziali per le piante. Nel tempo entrano in gioco anche foglie, radici e materia organica lasciata sul terreno.
È un principio usato da tempo nei sistemi agroforestali e documentato anche dalla FAO: alberi e colture possono condividere lo stesso spazio agricolo, con effetti sulla fertilità del terreno, sulla gestione dell’acqua e sulla protezione del suolo. A Udumka questa vecchia idea agricola viene rimessa al lavoro dentro un problema molto contemporaneo.
Le piogge, infatti, sono diventate più difficili da prevedere. CARE descrive precipitazioni violente, grandine e allagamenti capaci di compromettere i raccolti e impoverire ulteriormente terreni già sfruttati. Piantare una specie adatta, qui, significa cercare di lasciare qualcosa nel terreno anche quando l’acqua porta via il resto.
A pochi chilometri, cambiano anche le patate
Nel vicino villaggio di Kihesa Mgagao, Bariki Kagine coltivava patate con risultati scarsi e raccolti particolarmente vulnerabili alla grandine. Poi ha cominciato a cambiare diverse cose insieme: la distanza tra le piante, il momento della semina, l’uso delle previsioni meteorologiche, la fertilizzazione, la gestione dei parassiti e perfino la varietà coltivata. Ha scelto la Sagitta, più adatta al suo terreno. Il raccolto ottenuto gli ha fruttato circa 2 milioni di scellini tanzaniani, secondo quanto riportato da CARE.
È il risultato di un solo agricoltore, ma il cambiamento si vede bene: spostare una semina, lasciare più spazio tra le piante, scegliere una varietà diversa può fare la differenza quando il calendario delle piogge smette di comportarsi come prima. E infatti l’adattamento, da queste parti, ha un aspetto piuttosto poco spettacolare. Un albero nel posto giusto. Una patata piantata qualche giorno dopo. Un agricoltore che guarda le previsioni prima di entrare nel campo.
Il progetto punta a coinvolgere oltre 60 mila piccoli agricoltori
Her Resilience, Our Planet lavora nel bacino del Great Ruaha River, una delle aree agricole e naturali più importanti della Tanzania meridionale. Il programma è sostenuto anche da Global Affairs Canada e, secondo la scheda ufficiale del Governo canadese, proseguirà fino al 2030. CARE indica tra gli obiettivi oltre 60.000 piccoli agricoltori e 18.000 imprenditori agricoli coinvolti nella regione, con particolare attenzione a donne e giovani. Sono traguardi previsti dal progetto, non persone già raggiunte.
Per ora la storia è molto più piccola, ed è probabilmente per questo che funziona. Un vivaio gestito dal villaggio. Alberi scelti anche per ciò che fanno al terreno. Un agricoltore che cambia il modo di coltivare le patate e riesce a venderle meglio. Da Udumka non arriva una soluzione pronta per qualsiasi campo africano. Arriva qualcosa di più concreto: mentre il clima cambia le regole, questa comunità sta cambiando il modo di stare sul terreno. A volte cominciando da un albero.
Ti potrebbe interessare anche:
- Nei villaggi della Tanzania la crisi climatica si combatte con alveari, pollai e donne finalmente ammesse alle decisioni
- La crisi climatica si manifesta in modo differente in ciascun Paese: la campagna globale del clima nata dal basso e diffusa via Whatsapp
- In Burkina Faso hanno lasciato decidere alle donne come spendere i soldi per il clima: ora usano il 30% di legna in meno

title: In 2025, the ozone hole shrunk to one of its smallest sizes in decades
content:
The Antarctic ozone hole in 2025 was one of the smallest in decades—a testament to the continuing success of international action to protect Earth's ozone layer, which shields us from the sun's harmful ultraviolet rays, according to a new report from the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).
In welcome news, the WMO Ozone Bulletin said that last year's ozone hole ranked as the fourth or fifth smallest since severe depletion patterns were observed in 1992. This is the second consecutive year that both the depth and extent of the ozone hole were significantly below the 1990–2010 average.
Year-to-year fluctuations are influenced by large-scale meteorological transport conditions, which drive springtime ozone depletion almost every austral winter above Antarctica and every five to 10 years in the Northern Hemisphere.
In the Northern Hemisphere, total column ozone in 2025 was below average (negative anomalies) in a large region extending from Greenland and Europe to Central Asia, northern Japan and the Kamchatka Peninsula in the Russian Federation.
These variations occur within the long-term trend toward the healing of the ozone layer, reflecting the success of the Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer, which phased out chemicals such as chlorofluorocarbons once found in refrigeration, firefighting foam and other common uses.
"This is an environmental success story. Since 2000, the ozone layer has been recovering, and we can expect full recovery within several decades," said WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo.
The WMO Global Atmosphere Watch (GAW) network provides the critical, high-quality ground-based total column ozone observations required to accurately monitor ozone and ensure that long-term changes can be understood.
UV radiation
About 90% of atmospheric ozone resides in the upper stratosphere. If all this ozone were brought down to Earth's surface, the resulting layer of pure ozone would be only approximately 3 millimeters (0.12 inches) thick. Yet this thin layer blocks nearly all dangerous shortwave ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun and protects life on Earth.
While substantial progress has been made in addressing ozone depletion, measurements over the past decades show a significant increase in the number of days with high UV index values. The UV index was developed to track the depletion of the ozone layer and now serves as an international health standard for UV protection.
Since the mid-1990s, UV radiation has increased by as much as 20% in some parts of Europe. Ground-based measurements show that this has been driven primarily by a reduction in cloud cover and an accompanying increase in annual sunshine duration. Higher UV exposure means a greater risk of skin cancer and other UV-related diseases among exposed populations.
"In light of this trend, targeted and effective UV protection measures are of paramount importance," says the Bulletin.
World Ozone Day
The WMO Ozone Bulletin was released for World Ozone Day on Sept. 16, which celebrates the 1987 Montreal Protocol, which successfully phased out ozone-depleting substances. This year's theme is Global Action for a Cooler Planet, marking the 10th anniversary of the Kigali Amendment, which expanded the scope of the Montreal Protocol.
The 2016 Kigali Amendment provides for a phasedown of hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), potent greenhouse gases used to replace ozone-depleting substances. These chemicals are widely used in everyday cooling technologies such as refrigerators, air conditioners, insulating foams and some medical and industrial equipment.
While they do not deplete the ozone layer, some HFCs trap thousands of times more heat than carbon dioxide, even though they remain in the atmosphere for a much shorter time.
Over the past four decades, atmospheric measurements have demonstrated significant reductions in the concentrations of controlled ozone-depleting substances. But there have been unexpected emissions, for instance of CFC-11 until 2018 and HFC-23. This is why atmospheric monitoring remains essential to support targeted regulatory actions by national authorities.
The Ozone Bulletin draws attention to the state of the observing system, which traditionally relied primarily on Dobson and Brewer spectrophotometers. The number of active stations has gradually decreased from around 130 in the early 2000s to 110 today—with stations often closing in areas where observations are sparsest.
Next-generation array spectrometers have grown rapidly, but these focus on air quality measurements rather than stratospheric ozone monitoring.

title: Meta Expands Teen Safety With New Parental Supervision Features In India
content:
Meta has begun rolling out parental supervision on Threads across the Asia-Pacific region, including India, giving parents and guardians greater visibility and control over teenagers’ use of the platform.
The tools, available through Meta’s Family Centre, allow parents to view a teenager’s Threads usage for the previous seven days, set daily time limits, restrict access during specific hours, adjust night-time settings, manage tagging and oversee certain privacy and sensitive-content preferences.
The rollout, announced by Meta in September, builds on the platform’s existing Teen Accounts, which provide protections such as private-by-default accounts and restrictions on the content teens can see.
The move comes amid growing scrutiny of Meta in India over online child safety and the circulation of child sexual abuse material (CSAM). In July, the government said it had taken serious note of reports alleging advertisements linked to CSAM on social media and sought a detailed report from the concerned intermediary, while the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) also issued notices.
The NCPCR subsequently began a formal inquiry into alleged lapses in Meta India’s child-safety policies and summoned Meta India executives. In September, Meta agreed to report child-safety cases directly to India’s cybercrime authorities through the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), rather than relying solely on the previous reporting route through the US-based National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC).
Meta said, “protecting children on our platforms is a priority” and that it was committed to working with the government to ensure perpetrators are held responsible.
More Control For Parents
Under the new Threads supervision system, parents can view how much time their teenager has spent on the platform each day over the previous week, along with the average daily usage. They can set a daily limit and block Threads during selected days or hours. If a teenager accesses Threads on multiple devices, the time limit applies to their total usage rather than separately on each device.
Parents can also adjust Threads’ sleep mode, including limiting or blocking access at night. Meta says notifications are muted and auto-replies are enabled by default between 10 pm and 7 am under sleep mode. Parents can additionally control who can tag their teenager and manage or approve certain privacy settings and sensitive-content preferences.
The controls are being introduced alongside Threads’ existing Teen Accounts. Meta says parents can decide whether teenagers under 16 can make some of the platform’s default protections less restrictive. The company has described the supervision tools as an extension of safeguards already built into Teen Accounts, rather than a replacement for its existing moderation systems.
Scrutiny Over Child Safety
The India rollout comes against the backdrop of a wider dispute over how social-media platforms detect, remove and report material involving child sexual exploitation. In July, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology said the government had taken serious note of reports concerning advertisements allegedly linked to CSAM on social-media platforms and sought detailed information from the concerned intermediary. The PIB statement also noted that NCPCR had issued notices to the platforms involved.
The NCPCR later instituted a formal inquiry into alleged shortcomings in Meta India’s child-safety policies and its handling of CSAM-related material. Meta India Managing Director Arun Srinivas was summoned by the child-rights body as part of the proceedings. Reports said the inquiry followed concerns over Meta’s response to the allegations.
The issue subsequently led to a change in Meta’s reporting arrangement in India. Business Standard reported that Meta agreed to share child sexual abuse cases and details of repeat offenders directly with Indian law-enforcement agencies through the I4C cybercrime division. Government officials said such information could include account details such as names, associated email IDs and IP addresses, which they argued could assist investigations.
The government has also indicated that it expects greater accountability from major platforms. Government sources cited by Business Standard said Meta could not be viewed simply as an intermediary because its algorithms influence what content is amplified and made visible to users.
The Logical Indian’s Perspective
Children’s safety online cannot rest on one setting, one app or one technology. Meta’s parental supervision tools can give families greater visibility and help parents establish healthier boundaries around screen time, privacy and online interactions. At the same time, parental controls should complement — not substitute — the responsibility of platforms to detect harmful material, act swiftly on reports and cooperate transparently with authorities.
The recent scrutiny in India also highlights why child safety requires cooperation between parents, technology companies, regulators, child-rights bodies and law-enforcement agencies. Parents need practical tools, teenagers need age-appropriate protection and platforms need systems that respond effectively when those safeguards fail.
